definition_zh: 质子；原子核中带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子；氢原子核
definition_en: a stable particle found in every atomic nucleus, carrying one unit of positive electric charge
core_image: 一颗带正电的小球被一层中和的云裹着，云散开后它独自露出来，仍牢牢占着中心的位置
scene: 云室里，宇宙射线留下一条粗短的白色轨迹。A proton knocked loose by a cosmic ray left a thick track in the cloud chamber.
sceneCN: 这里 proton 指「原子核中带正电的粒子」（第 1 个义项：原子核内带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子）；句意：一个被宇宙射线撞出的质子在云室里留下一条粗而短的轨迹。图中可辨识物件：云室、铅板、白色轨迹、实验台。

derivatives.zh: 使质子化；向分子加入质子

senses.title: The positive particle of the nucleus
senses.titleCN: 原子核中带正电的粒子
senses.definition: the stable particle that carries one unit of positive charge inside an atomic nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 原子核内部带一个单位正电荷的稳定粒子
senses.example: Every nucleus except ordinary hydrogen holds at least one proton.
senses.exampleCN: 除普通氢以外，每一种原子核都至少含有一个质子。
senses.why: The Greek name means 'first', and the proton was the first nuclear particle to be identified, so it took that name.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词本义为「第一」，而质子是最早被辨认出的核内粒子，因此得了这个名字。

senses.title: A hydrogen nucleus on its own
senses.definition: a hydrogen nucleus stripped of its electron, which is exactly one proton
senses.definitionCN: 失去电子后的氢原子核，也就是单独的一个质子
senses.example: Strip the electron from a hydrogen atom and only a proton remains.
senses.exampleCN: 把电子从氢原子上剥离，剩下的就只有质子。
senses.why: Hydrogen is the one element whose nucleus is a single proton, so the general name also names that simplest case.
senses.whyCN: 氢是唯一核内只有一个质子的元素，因此这个通名也直接指最简单的那个情形。

senses.title: The count that fixes an element
senses.titleCN: 决定元素身份的那个数量
senses.definition: the number of protons in a nucleus, which determines which chemical element it is
senses.definitionCN: 原子核中的质子数目，决定它属于哪种化学元素
senses.example: Add one proton and the element changes into the next one in the table.
senses.exampleCN: 增加一个质子，元素就变成周期表里的下一种。
senses.why: A chemical reaction may move electrons but never changes this count, so the count became the identity card of an element.
senses.whyCN: 化学反应可以搬动电子，却改不了这个数目，于是这个数目成了元素的身份证明。

senses.title: A hydrogen ion in acid chemistry
senses.titleCN: 酸化学里被交出的氢离子
senses.definition: a bare hydrogen ion that an acid gives away to another substance
senses.definitionCN: 酸交给另一种物质的裸氢离子
senses.example: In the modern definition, an acid is any substance that can give up a proton.
senses.exampleCN: 按现代定义，凡能交出一个质子的物质都是酸。
senses.why: A hydrogen ion without its electron is a proton, so chemistry borrowed the nuclear name for the thing an acid hands over.
senses.whyCN: 失去电子的氢离子就是一个质子，因此化学界借用了核物理的称呼，来指酸交出的那个东西。

senses.title: A beam aimed at a tumour
senses.titleCN: 用于治疗肿瘤的质子束
senses.definition: a stream of accelerated protons used as a medical tool that can be stopped at a chosen depth
senses.definitionCN: 把质子加速成束，作为能在选定深度停下的医疗工具
senses.example: The clinic chose proton treatment because the beam stops inside the tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所选用质子治疗，因为粒子束会在肿瘤内部停下。
senses.why: Protons lose energy in a predictable way, so a beam can be aimed to spare the healthy tissue behind it.
senses.whyCN: 质子的能量损失有可预测的规律，因此束流可以被瞄准，从而避开其后方的健康组织。

senses.title: A fast visitor from space
senses.titleCN: 从太空高速到访的质子
senses.definition: a high-energy proton arriving from outer space as part of cosmic radiation
senses.definitionCN: 作为宇宙辐射的一部分，从外层空间高速抵达的高能质子
senses.example: A single cosmic proton can trigger a shower of secondary particles.
senses.exampleCN: 一个宇宙质子就能引发一连串次级粒子。
senses.why: Cosmic rays are mostly protons, so astronomy uses the ordinary nuclear word for these travellers.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙射线主要由质子组成，天文学便用这个平常的核物理词来称呼这些远行者。

senses.title: The charged stream of the solar wind
senses.titleCN: 太阳风里的带电粒子流
senses.definition: one of the charged particles that the sun continuously sends out into space
senses.definitionCN: 太阳持续抛向太空的带电粒子之一
senses.example: The solar wind is a thin gas of protons and electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳风是质子与电子组成的稀薄气体。
senses.why: The solar wind is ionized hydrogen, so its positive half is simply protons.
senses.whyCN: 太阳风是电离的氢，其中带正电的那一半就是质子。

senses.title: The fuel of the proton chain in stars
senses.definition: a proton taking part in the fusion chain that powers stars like the sun
senses.definitionCN: 参与聚变链式反应、为太阳这类恒星供能的质子
senses.example: Four protons must combine before one helium nucleus appears in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 在太阳内部，要四个质子合起来才会出现一个氦核。
senses.why: The chain of reactions begins with protons, so the whole stellar process is named after them.
senses.whyCN: 这条反应链从质子开始，因此整个恒星过程以它命名。

intro.en: Proton is Greek, built from prōtos 'first' with the particle ending -on that physics later fixed in place. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语词，由「第一」加粒子命名惯用的词尾构成；年代均为约数。

items.en: Prōtos meant 'first, foremost', built on pro 'before, in front'. Its deeper origin is not reconstructed with confidence.
items.cn: prōtos 意为「第一、最前的」，由表示「在前」的成分构成。它更早的来源无法稳妥地重构。

items.en: The neuter form prōton meant 'the first thing'. Ancient writers used it for a first principle, long before physics existed.
items.cn: 中性形式 prōton 意为「第一者」。古代作者用它指第一原理，远在物理学出现之前。

items.en: When the lightest nucleus was identified around 1919 to 1920, the old word for a first thing was revived for it.
items.cn: 大约在 1919 至 1920 年间最轻的核被确认时，这个表示「第一者」的旧词被重新启用。

items.en: As the neutron was named by contrast, the positive partner kept the name proton, and the pair became the two nucleons.
items.cn: 中子作为对照被命名后，带正电的搭档保留质子之名，两者合称核子。

items.en: The first recorded uses for the modern particle sense are approximate; the word itself is ancient, the meaning is about a century old.
items.cn: 现代粒子义的最早书证年代为约数；词本身古老，而这一含义只有约一百年。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to proton but come from other roots; group two holds the particles it is measured against.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近却另有词源的词；第二组是常与它相比较的其他粒子。

entries.definition: From Greek phōs, phōtos 'light' plus the same particle ending: a quantum of light, with no charge at all.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语「光」加同一个粒子结尾构成：光的一个量子，完全不带电荷。

entries.definition: Coined from Greek prōteios 'primary', which rests on the same prōtos 'first': a primary substance of living tissue, not a particle.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语「首要的」造出，而这个词又出自同一个「第一」：指生命组织的首要成分，与粒子无关。

entries.definition: Greek prōtos 'first' plus agōnistēs 'competitor': the leading figure in a drama, from the same first-word root.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「第一」加「竞争者」：戏剧中的首要人物，与质子的「第一」同源。

entries.definition: Greek prōtos 'first' plus typos 'impression': the first model of a thing, not a nuclear particle.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「第一」加「印痕」：某物的首个模型，与核粒子无关。

entries.definition: The nucleon with almost the same mass and no electric charge; proton and neutron together make up nearly all nuclear mass.
entries.definitionCN: 质量几乎相同但不带电的核子；质子与中子共同构成几乎全部核质量。

entries.definition: The light negative particle that orbits the nucleus; its charge balances the proton's charge in a neutral atom.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕原子核运动的轻质负电粒子；在中性原子里，它的电荷与质子相抵。

entries.definition: The covering word for either kind of nuclear particle, so a proton is one sort of nucleon.
entries.definitionCN: 对两种核内粒子的统称，因此质子是核子的一种。

entries.definition: A whole atom or molecule that has gained or lost electrons; a lone proton is the smallest positive ion.
entries.definitionCN: 获得或失去电子的整个原子或分子；单独的质子是最小的正离子。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek prōtos 'first' plus the particle ending -on: the first particle of the nucleus.
normal.cn: 希腊语「第一」加粒子结尾：核内第一个被认出的粒子。

normal.en: The proton sets the element's number, so its count is the identity of the atom.
normal.cn: 质子数决定元素，因此这个数目就是原子的身份。

normal.en: The family runs proton, protonic, protonate, protonation, antiproton.
normal.cn: 同族词包括质子、质子的、使质子化、质子化、反质子。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its uses: proton beam, proton therapy, proton donor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：质子束、质子治疗、质子供体。

normal.en: The same first-root appears in protein, protagonist and prototype, all from Greek prōtos.
normal.cn: 同一个「第一」词根出现在蛋白质、主角与原型中，都出自希腊语。

abstract.en: Picture a numbered seat that decides which row the whole theatre belongs to.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带编号的座位，它决定整个剧场属于哪一排。

abstract.en: Picture one lamp at the centre of a dark hall, giving light but never taking it.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗大厅中央的一盏灯，只给光，不取光。

abstract.en: Picture the first brick laid, whose position names the wall that follows.
abstract.cn: 想象砌下的第一块砖，它的位置为后面整堵墙命名。

examples.en: The nucleus of carbon holds six protons and six neutrons.
examples.cn: 碳的原子核含六个质子与六个中子。

examples.en: Chemists describe an acid as a proton donor.
examples.cn: 化学家把酸描述为质子供体。

examples.en: The sun burns by turning protons into helium.
examples.cn: 太阳靠把质子变成氦来发光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（在前）+ ton（吨）」——最前面那块最重的砖，就是质子

root: 希腊 prōtos「第一」+ 粒子命名惯用的词尾；prōtos 更早的来源不明。英语形式即本词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the charged core of the atom, move to the bare hydrogen nucleus and the element count, then follow the same particle into acids, hospitals, cosmic rays, the solar wind and finally the sun's fusion chain.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从原子带正电的核心出发，转到单独的氢核与元素编号，再让同一个粒子依次进入酸、医院、宇宙射线、太阳风，最后进入太阳的聚变链。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one positively charged brick at the centre of every atom, and the same brick alone in the simplest atom.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个原子中心一块带正电的砖，而在最简单的原子里只有这一块砖。

branches.en: ONE BRICK: whether inside a heavy nucleus or alone as hydrogen, the same charged brick is being named.
branches.cn: 同一块砖：无论在重核内部还是单独作为氢，被命名的都是这块带正电的砖。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: the count of bricks is written down as the name of the element.
branches.cn: 账本：砖的数目被记成元素的名称。

branches.en: THE HANDOVER: chemistry treats the brick as a token that an acid gives away.
branches.cn: 交出：化学把这颗砖当作酸可以递出去的凭物。

branches.en: THE TRAVELLER: the same brick is aimed at a tumour, arrives from space, or streams out of the sun.
branches.cn: 远行者：同一颗砖或被瞄准肿瘤，或从太空抵达，或从太阳流出。

branches.en: THE FURNACE: in stars the brick becomes fuel, and four of them must meet to make helium.
branches.cn: 熔炉：在恒星里这砖成了燃料，四颗相会才能造出氦。

intro.en: Proton is a Greek noun, but its first-root and its particle ending both recur across scientific and everyday English.
intro.cn: 质子是希腊语名词，但它的「第一」词根与粒子结尾在科学与日常英语里都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate of proton; the Latin word for first, primus, belongs to another family. The Greek forms below are the true parts.
latinIntro.cn: 质子没有拉丁同族词；拉丁语里表示「第一」的 primus 属于另一个词族。真正的构件是下面的希腊语形式。

items.example: The prefix marks whatever comes first in a series.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出系列中最先出现的那一个。

items.example: The adjective ranks one item ahead of all others.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把某一项排在所有其他项之前。

items.example: The proton sits at the centre of the atom.
items.exampleCN: 质子位于原子的中心。

items.example: The protonic charge balances the electron cloud.
items.exampleCN: 质子的电荷与电子云相抵。

items.meaning: to add a proton to a molecule
items.example: The acid protonates the base within microseconds.
items.exampleCN: 酸在微秒之内就使碱质子化。

items.meaning: a primary substance of living tissue
items.meaningCN: 生命组织里的首要成分
items.example: Protein was named as the first substance of the body.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质曾被命名为身体的首要物质。

items.example: The protagonist speaks first in every act.
items.exampleCN: 主角在每一幕里都最先开口。

items.meaning: the first model of a device
items.example: The prototype was tested before any copies were made.
items.exampleCN: 原型在任何复制品造出之前先接受了测试。

definition_zh: 中子；原子核中不带电的粒子；中子星中的致密物质成分
definition_en: a nuclear particle with almost the same mass as a proton but no electric charge
core_image: 一颗与质子几乎同样重的小球从秤上走过，电荷表却始终指着零
scene: 反应堆的水池边，仪器记录到一个不带电的粒子撞进铀核。A slow neutron split the uranium nucleus and started a chain of reactions.
sceneCN: 这里 neutron 指「原子核中不带电的粒子」（第 1 个义项：质量与质子相近但不带电荷的核粒子）；句意：一个慢中子在铀核上引发裂变，并开启了一连串反应。图中可辨识物件：水池、铀棒、探测器、计数屏。

derivatives.zh: 中子物质（假想的纯中子物质）

senses.title: The charge-free nucleon
senses.definition: the nuclear particle that has nearly the mass of a proton but carries no electric charge
senses.definitionCN: 质量接近质子、但不带电荷的核粒子
senses.example: A helium nucleus contains two protons and two neutrons.
senses.exampleCN: 一个氦核含两个质子与两个中子。
senses.why: Latin neuter means 'neither of the two', and this particle is neither positive nor negative, so the name records its missing charge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「两者皆非」正好描述这颗既不正也不负的粒子，名字记下的就是它缺了电荷。

senses.title: The mass that names an isotope
senses.titleCN: 决定同位素编号的那部分质量
senses.definition: the count of neutrons that, added to the proton count, gives the mass number of an isotope
senses.definitionCN: 中子数目与质子数目相加，得出某种同位素的质量数
senses.example: Carbon-14 carries two more neutrons than the common form of carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 碳十四比常见的碳多两个中子。
senses.why: Protons fix the element while neutrons vary, so the neutron count is what separates one isotope from another.
senses.whyCN: 质子固定元素，中子却可变，因此中子数正是区分同位素的那一项。

senses.title: A free neutron that falls apart
senses.definition: a neutron outside a nucleus, which decays within minutes into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino
senses.definitionCN: 脱离原子核的中子，会在几分钟内衰变成一个质子、一个电子与一个反中微子
senses.example: A free neutron lasts only about a quarter of an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 自由中子只存在大约一刻钟。
senses.why: Outside the stabilizing grip of a nucleus the neutron is unstable, and this slow decay became a standard example of beta decay.
senses.whyCN: 离开原子核的稳定约束后中子会变得不稳定，这一缓慢衰变成了贝塔衰变的标准例子。

senses.title: The trigger of a chain reaction
senses.definition: a neutron that enters a heavy nucleus and causes it to split, releasing further neutrons
senses.definitionCN: 进入重核并使其裂开、同时放出更多中子的粒子
senses.example: One neutron can start a chain that releases enormous heat.
senses.exampleCN: 一个中子就能开启释放巨大热量的链式反应。
senses.why: Because it carries no charge, a neutron can approach a nucleus without being pushed away, which makes it the ideal trigger.
senses.whyCN: 不带电的中子不会被原子核排斥，因此成为最理想的引发者。

senses.title: The probe for hidden atoms
senses.definition: a neutron used in scattering or diffraction experiments to locate light atoms that X-rays barely see
senses.definitionCN: 在散射或衍射实验中用来定位轻原子的中子，而这类原子用射线很难看清
senses.example: Neutron scattering showed where the hydrogen atoms sat in the lattice.
senses.exampleCN: 中子散射显示出氢原子在晶格中的位置。
senses.why: Neutrons scatter off nuclei rather than electrons, so they reveal hydrogen, which is nearly invisible to other probes.
senses.whyCN: 中子与原子核而非电子发生散射，因此能显示几乎对其他探针隐形的氢。

senses.title: The matter of a neutron star
senses.definition: the densely packed neutron matter left behind when a massive star collapses
senses.definitionCN: 大质量恒星坍缩后留下的致密中子物质
senses.example: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh as much as a mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 一茶匙中子星物质就会重如一座山。
senses.why: Gravity crushes electrons and protons together into neutrons, so the star is described by the particle it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 引力把电子与质子压成中子，因此这颗星就用构成它的粒子来命名。

senses.title: The particle slowed on purpose
senses.definition: a neutron reduced in speed by a moderator so that it is more likely to split uranium
senses.definitionCN: 经慢化剂降低速度、从而更容易引发铀裂变的中子
senses.example: Water acts as a moderator because it slows neutrons without absorbing too many.
senses.exampleCN: 水充当慢化剂，因为它让中子减速，又不会吸收太多。
senses.why: Slow neutrons spend more time near a nucleus and are far more likely to be captured, so reactors deliberately slow them.
senses.whyCN: 慢中子在核旁停留更久，被俘获的机会大得多，因此反应堆有意让它减速。

senses.title: The burst of a neutron weapon
senses.titleCN: 中子武器释放的高速粒子流
senses.definition: a flux of fast neutrons produced by a small nuclear device designed to irradiate rather than flatten
senses.definitionCN: 由小型核装置产生的高速中子流，其设计目的是辐照而非摧毁建筑
senses.example: The neutron bomb was meant to leave buildings standing.
senses.exampleCN: 中子弹的设计意图是让建筑物保持不倒。
senses.why: Weapons that emphasize this particle rather than blast heat were named after it, since the prompt radiation does the damage.
senses.whyCN: 这种武器强调粒子而非爆炸热，由于造成伤害的是瞬时辐射，便以该粒子命名。

intro.en: Neutron joins Latin neuter 'neither' to the -on ending already used in proton and electron. The particle was named in the early 1930s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语「两者皆非」接到已在质子、电子里使用的同一个词尾上；这个粒子在二十世纪三十年代初获得命名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Neuter is ne 'not' plus uter 'either of two', so it means 'neither the one nor the other'.
items.cn: neuter 由「不」加「两者之一」构成，意为「两者都不是」。

items.en: Grammarians already used neuter for the gender that is neither masculine nor feminine, a ready-made label for a charge that is neither positive nor negative.
items.cn: 语法学家早已用这个词指既非阳性也非阴性的中性，正好可以用来标出既不正也不负的电荷。

items.en: In the early 1930s the neutral particle found in nuclear reactions took the name neutron, following the pattern of proton and electron.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十年代初，核反应中发现的不带电粒子依照质子与电子的构词方式得名中子。

items.en: With the first chain reactions the word spread into engineering: slow neutron, moderator, neutron number all date from this period.
items.cn: 随着最初的链式反应，这个词进入工程领域：慢中子、慢化剂、中子数都出自这一时期。

items.en: The 1960s added neutron star to the language, extending the particle's name to a whole kind of collapsed star.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代又添了「中子星」，把这一粒子的名字扩展到一整类坍缩恒星。

items.en: Exact first citations for the technical compounds are approximate; the core word and its Latin base are well recorded.
items.cn: 各技术复合词的最早书证年代为约数；核心词及其拉丁语来源都有充分记录。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that share the neutral idea or merely the ending; group two holds the nuclear particles it is balanced against.
note.cn: 第一组是共享「中性」概念或仅仅共享词尾的形近词；第二组是常与它对照的核粒子。

entries.definition: Coined in Italian as a diminutive of neutro 'neutral': a tiny neutral particle with almost no mass, named by analogy, not by descent from neutron.
entries.definitionCN: 在意大利语里由「中性的」加指小成分造出：一种几乎没有质量的中性小粒子，是类比命名，并非从中子派生。

entries.definition: The Latin adjective itself, used in English for the neither gender or for a neutered animal; it is the direct source of the particle's first element.
entries.definitionCN: 就是那个拉丁形容词，英语里指中性性别或已绝育的动物；它是这个粒子词首成分的直接来源。

entries.definition: From the same ne plus uter stock: neither side in a dispute, or no net charge in physics.
entries.definitionCN: 出自同一「不」加「两者之一」的词源：争执中不站任何一方，物理上指没有净电荷。

entries.definition: From Greek neuron 'sinew, nerve': a nerve cell, sharing the ending only and nothing of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊语「筋、神经」：指神经细胞，只共享词尾，与词根无关。

entries.definition: The positively charged nucleon of the same mass; together they form the nucleus and are called nucleons.
entries.definitionCN: 质量相同而带正电的核子；两者共同构成原子核，合称核子。

entries.definition: The covering name for a proton or a neutron, used when the distinction between them does not matter.
entries.definitionCN: 质子或中子的统称，在不需要区分两者时使用。

entries.definition: The very light negative particle of the atom; unlike the neutron it is not a nucleon and does not sit in the nucleus.
entries.definitionCN: 原子中极轻的负电粒子；与中子不同，它不是核子，也不住在核内。

entries.definition: A short-lived particle made of a quark and an antiquark; the ending is shared, the constitution is entirely different.
entries.definitionCN: 由一个夸克与一个反夸克组成的短命粒子；词尾相同，构成却完全不同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin neuter 'neither' plus the -on ending: the particle that is neither positive nor negative.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「两者皆非」加同一个粒子词尾：既不正也不负的粒子。

normal.en: The family runs neutron, neutronic, antineutron, neutronium, neutron-rich.
normal.cn: 同族词包括中子、中子的、反中子、中子物质、富中子的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its roles: neutron star, neutron scattering, neutron moderator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：中子星、中子散射、中子慢化剂。

normal.en: Isotopes are told apart by their neutron number, not by their proton number.
normal.cn: 区分同位素靠中子数，而不是质子数。

normal.en: The same neutral root appears in neuter, neutral and neutrino, though the last is an Italian coinage.
normal.cn: 同一个「中性」词根出现在中性、中立的词与中微子里，不过最后一个是在意大利语里造的。

abstract.en: Picture a guest of the same weight as the host who pays no entrance fee of charge.
abstract.cn: 想象一位与主人同样重、却不用交电荷门票的客人。

abstract.en: Picture a key with no metal that still opens the heavy door because nothing pushes it back.
abstract.cn: 想象一把没有金属的钥匙，因为不会被推回，照样打开重门。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that reads the same weight twice but shows zero on the charge dial.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤两次读出同样的重量，电荷表盘却始终是零。

examples.en: Ordinary hydrogen has a nucleus of one proton and no neutron.
examples.cn: 普通氢的原子核只有一个质子，没有中子。

examples.en: Boron absorbs a neutron and becomes a different isotope.
examples.cn: 硼吸收一个中子后变成另一种同位素。

examples.en: Neutron stars are the leftover cores of exploded massive stars.
examples.cn: 中子星是爆发后的大质量恒星留下的核心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「neutral（中性）」的核里那颗球——既不吸也不斥，就是中子

root: 拉丁 neuter「两者皆非」= ne「不」+ uter「两者之一」；加 -on 粒子结尾。英语 neutron。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chargeless particle: first the nuclear member and the isotope count, then its solitary decay, its work as a trigger, a probe, a star's material, a deliberately slowed tool and finally a weapon's burst.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一颗不带电的粒子走：先是核内成员与同位素计数，再是它的孤独衰变、作为引发者、作为探针、作为恒星材料、被人为减速的工具，最后是武器释放的粒子流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball of the same weight as its neighbour that never registers on the charge dial.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗与邻居同样重、却从不在电荷表上留下读数的小球。

branches.en: THE BALLAST: inside the nucleus the neutron adds weight and no charge, and its number separates isotopes.
branches.cn: 压舱物：在核内它只添重量不添电荷，其数目把同位素分开。

branches.en: THE LONER: once outside the nucleus it cannot hold itself together and falls into a proton and an electron.
branches.cn: 孤独者：一旦离开原子核，它维持不住自己，裂成一个质子与一个电子。

branches.en: THE KEY: no charge means no repulsion, so the neutron can enter a nucleus and split it, especially when slowed.
branches.cn: 钥匙：不带电就不被排斥，因此能进入核内使之裂开，减速之后尤其容易。

branches.en: THE LANTERN: scattering off nuclei lets it show where hydrogen hides.
branches.cn: 灯：与原子核散射，使它照出氢藏在何处。

branches.en: THE EXTREME: crushed into a star it becomes the matter itself, and released in a burst it becomes a weapon's edge.
branches.cn: 极端：被压进恒星时它成为物质本身，被成束放出时又成为武器的锋刃。

intro.en: Neutron is a Latin-based coinage: a Latin adjective of neutrality plus the scientific ending shared with proton and electron.
intro.cn: 中子是以拉丁语为基础的造词：一个表示中性的拉丁形容词，加上与质子、电子共享的科学词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin neuter and its root uter also yield neuter, neutral and neutrality in English; the particle ending -on was added by physicists.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的中性形式及其词根还衍生出英语里的中性、中立的与中立状态；粒子结尾则由物理学家加上。

items.example: The negative particle turns an either-or word into a neither word.
items.exampleCN: 这个否定小品词把「二者之一」变成「二者皆非」。

items.structure: uter, utra, utrum (Latin adjective, 'either of two')
items.example: The adjective asks which of two things is meant.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用来问两者之中指哪一个。

items.meaning: neither the one nor the other
items.example: The neuter form belongs to neither of the other two.
items.exampleCN: 中性形式不属于另外两者中的任何一个。

items.meaning: taking no side; having no net charge
items.meaningCN: 不站边的；没有净电荷的
items.example: A neutral atom balances its charges.
items.exampleCN: 中性原子使电荷保持平衡。

items.example: The neutron carries no charge at all.
items.exampleCN: 中子完全不带电荷。

items.example: Neutronic analysis predicts the reactor's behaviour.
items.exampleCN: 中子学分析可预测反应堆的行为。

items.example: The neutrino passes through matter almost untouched.
items.exampleCN: 中微子几乎不受阻碍地穿过物质。

items.example: An antineutron annihilates on contact with a neutron.
items.exampleCN: 反中子一碰到中子便湮灭。

latinEntries.meaning: which of the two; either of the two

definition_zh: 粒子；微粒；极少量；语法中的小品词；物理学中的基本粒子
definition_en: an extremely small piece of matter, or a very small unit treated as a physical or grammatical entity
core_image: 阳光斜穿暗室，空气里飘着一粒极小的灰，亮一下又沉下去
scene: 一束阳光斜穿暗室，空气里有一点灰烬在发亮。A single particle of soot drifted across the beam of light.
sceneCN: 这里 particle 指「极小的物质颗粒」（第 1 个义项：肉眼几乎看不见的一小块物质）；句意：一粒烟灰在光柱中缓缓飘过。图中可辨识物件：光柱、悬浮的灰点、暗室、窗缝。

derivatives.zh: 特定的；讲究的（原义「属于某一小部分的」）
颗粒物（空气污染物指标）

senses.title: A tiny piece of matter
senses.definition: an extremely small piece of solid matter that can be seen only with effort or not at all
senses.definitionCN: 极小的固体物质，肉眼几乎看不见或完全看不见
senses.example: A particle of dust settled on the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 一粒灰尘落在镜片上。
senses.why: Latin particula is a diminutive of pars 'part', so the word begins as 'a little part' and keeps that literal smallness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原词是「部分」的指小形式，因此这个词从一开始就是「一小部分」，并保留了这个字面意义。

senses.title: A basic unit in physics
senses.definition: a distinct unit of matter or energy treated as an individual entity, such as an electron or a photon
senses.definitionCN: 被当作独立个体处理的一份物质或能量，如电子或光子
senses.example: The accelerator smashes particles together at nearly the speed of light.
senses.exampleCN: 加速器让粒子以接近光速相互撞击。
senses.why: Physics generalized the little-part idea until it meant the smallest countable unit, whether or not it has mass.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把「小部分」推广成「最小可数单元」，无论它是否有质量。

senses.title: A fragment emitted in radiation
senses.titleCN: 放射过程中放出的碎片
senses.definition: a small piece of matter thrown out by a radioactive nucleus, such as an alpha or beta particle
senses.definitionCN: 放射性原子核抛出的微小物质，如阿尔法粒子或贝塔粒子
senses.example: An alpha particle is two protons and two neutrons bound together.
senses.exampleCN: 一个阿尔法粒子就是两个质子与两个中子结合在一起。
senses.why: Early radiation research saw only anonymous specks flying off, so these fragments were simply called particles until they were identified.
senses.whyCN: 早期放射研究只看到无名的小东西飞出，因此在被辨认之前，这些碎片就径称粒子。

senses.title: A short grammatical word
senses.definition: a short word with little meaning of its own that marks a grammatical relation, such as a preposition or a phrasal-verb adverb
senses.definitionCN: 本身意义很弱、用来标记语法关系的短词，如介词或短语动词中的副词
senses.example: The particle 'up' changes the meaning of the verb.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小品词就能改变整个动词的意思。
senses.why: Grammarians borrowed the word for an uninflected scrap of language that behaves like a loose piece rather than a full word.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家借这个词来指不变化的小语言片段，因为它像一块散件，而不像一个完整的词。

senses.title: The word that carries negation
senses.definition: a grammatical element that marks negation, such as 'not' or the negative prefix un-
senses.definitionCN: 标记否定的语法成分，如表示否定的副词或否定前缀
senses.example: In some languages a single particle turns a statement into a denial.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言里，一个小品词就能把陈述变成否认。
senses.why: Negation is often carried by one small fixed word, so the general 'small piece' label settled on it in descriptive grammar.
senses.whyCN: 否定常由一个固定的小词承担，因此描述语法时就把「小片段」这一称呼安在它身上。

senses.title: A minute amount of a quality
senses.titleCN: 某种品质的极微小分量
senses.definition: a very small amount of a quality such as truth, doubt or humour
senses.definitionCN: 真、疑、幽默等品质的极小分量
senses.example: There is not a particle of evidence for the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法没有丝毫证据。
senses.why: The literal speck became a measure of anything that can be divided, so a particle of truth is the smallest imaginable share of it.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的微粒变成衡量可分之物的一把尺，因此「一颗粒子的真相」就是想象中最小的份额。

senses.title: Airborne particulate pollution
senses.definition: one of the fine solid bits suspended in air that are counted as pollution, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 悬浮在空气中、被计入污染的细小固体，通常用复数
senses.example: The city measures particles smaller than two and a half microns.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市测量小于两点五微米的颗粒。
senses.why: Air-quality rules needed a countable unit for soot and smoke, and the everyday word for a speck supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 空气质量规则需要给烟尘一个可计数的单位，日常表示微粒的词正好补上。

senses.title: The smallest separable unit of an idea
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：一个想法中最小可分的单位
senses.definition: the smallest piece into which an argument, a story or a system can be divided without losing its identity
senses.definitionCN: 论证、故事或体系在不失去自身特性的前提下能分到的最小单位
senses.example: He rebuilt the theory from its smallest particles of fact.
senses.exampleCN: 他从事实的最小颗粒出发重建了这套理论。
senses.why: The abstract sense treats ideas as matter: anything analysable can be ground down to particles and put back together.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把想法当成物质：凡可分析之物都能磨成颗粒，再重新拼起。

intro.en: Particle comes from Latin particula, a diminutive of pars 'part', through Old French. The smallness is built into the form itself. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: particle 经古法语来自拉丁 particula，而 particula 是「部分」的指小形式。小，是这个词形自带的意思。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pars meant 'part, piece, share'. Its deeper origin is not established beyond the Latin stage.
items.cn: pars 意为「部分、片段、份额」。越过拉丁语阶段之后，它的更早来源没有定论。

items.en: The diminutive suffix made particula 'a little part', a word used for a crumb, a scrap or a small article.
items.cn: 指小后缀造出 particula「一小部分」，用来指碎屑、碎片或小件物品。

items.en: Old French particule carried the word into English, where it first named a small piece of matter or a fragment of a substance.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带进英语，最初指一小块物质或某物的一小片。

items.en: By the sixteenth century grammarians had applied it to uninflected function words, giving the sense still used in language teaching.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，语法学家已把它用于不变化的虚词，形成语言教学中仍在使用的义项。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century the word named the units revealed by atomic and nuclear research, and particle physics became a discipline.
items.cn: 从十九世纪末起，这个词用来指原子与核研究揭示出的单元，粒子物理学逐渐成为一门学科。

items.en: The first dates for the grammar and physics senses are approximate; the Latin noun itself is fully attested.
items.cn: 语法义与物理义的最早年代为约数；拉丁名词本身有完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin part-root or with a similar shape; group two holds size words that overlap with particle in ordinary use.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「部分」词根或形状相近的词；第二组是日常使用中与这个词重叠的尺寸词。

entries.definition: From Latin participium, which joins pars 'part' with capere 'to take': a verb form that takes part in two grammatical roles, not a small piece.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁语，把「部分」与「拿取」合起来：指兼有两种语法角色的动词形式，并非小碎片。

entries.definition: Built on the same little-part stock: one specific item singled out, hence detailed or fussy.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「小部分」词源：被单挑出来的某一项，因此引申为具体的、讲究的。

entries.definition: From pars plus -al: only a part of the whole, or favouring one side.
entries.definitionCN: 由「部分」加形容词后缀构成：只是整体的一部分，或偏向一方。

entries.definition: From Latin portio 'share', a relative of pars: an allotted share, usually of something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「份额」，与「部分」同族：指分得的一份，通常属于更大之物。

entries.definition: The smallest unit of a chemical element; it contains many particles and is not itself a fragment.
entries.definitionCN: 化学元素的最小单元；它内部含许多粒子，本身并不是碎片。

entries.definition: Two or more atoms bonded together; it is a structured group rather than a loose speck.
entries.definitionCN: 两个或多个原子结合成的整体；它是有结构的一组，而非松散的一粒。

entries.definition: An ordinary word for a tiny spot or crumb, usually visible; it lacks the technical range of particle.
entries.definitionCN: 日常指可见的小点或碎屑，不含这个粒子词的技术含义。

entries.definition: A small hard piece such as a seed or a grain of sand; it suggests something solid and countable.
entries.definitionCN: 像种子或沙粒那样的小硬块；暗示实体且可数。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin pars 'part' plus a diminutive suffix: a little part.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「部分」加指小后缀：一小部分。

normal.en: The family runs particle, particulate, particular, partial, portion.
normal.cn: 同族词包括粒子、颗粒状的、特定的、部分的、份额。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical sense: particle physics, particle accelerator, alpha particle.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：粒子物理学、粒子加速器、阿尔法粒子。

normal.en: Grammar uses the same word for little words like up, not and to.
normal.cn: 语法里用同一个词指那些表示方向、否定或连接的小词。

normal.en: Air-quality reports count particles, which is the literal sense applied to pollution.
normal.cn: 空气质量报告清点颗粒物，正是字面义用在污染上。

abstract.en: Picture a single speck held in a sunbeam, the only thing visible in an empty room.
abstract.cn: 想象光柱里悬着一粒灰，空屋里唯一可见的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence taken apart until only the smallest unchangeable words remain.
abstract.cn: 想象把一句话拆开，直到只剩不可再分的小词。

abstract.en: Picture a proof ground down to its smallest facts and rebuilt from them.
abstract.cn: 想象把一套论证磨成最小的事实颗粒，再由这些颗粒重建。

examples.en: Filters catch particles that the eye cannot see.
examples.cn: 过滤器能截住肉眼看不见的颗粒。

examples.en: Physicists sort particles by mass and charge.
examples.cn: 物理学家按质量与电荷给粒子分类。

examples.en: The report found not a particle of proof.
examples.cn: 报告找不到丝毫证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「part（部分）+ icle（小）」——整体里的一小部分，就是粒子

root: 拉丁 pars「部分」+ 指小后缀 -cula → particula「一小部分」。pars 更早来源不明。英语 particle。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep the literal smallness but change the scale: a speck of dust, a unit of physics, a radiation fragment, a grammar word, a negative marker, a shred of evidence, a pollution count and finally the smallest piece of an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留字面上的「小」，只是换了尺度：一粒灰、一个物理单元、一块放射碎片、一个语法小词、一个否定标记、一丝证据、一项污染计数，最后是一个想法的最小碎片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one speck visible in a sunbeam, small enough to be almost nothing yet countable.
core.cn: 核心意象：光柱里可见的一粒灰，小得几乎不存在，却仍能数出来。

branches.en: THE SPECK: dust in a room and soot in the air are the same literal little piece, one domestic and one regulated.
branches.cn: 微粒：屋里的灰与空中的烟尘是同一个字面小片，一个家常，一个受管制。

branches.en: THE UNIT: physics turns the speck into a countable entity, and radiation research turns it into a named fragment.
branches.cn: 单元：物理学把微粒变成可计数实体，放射研究把它变成有名目的碎片。

branches.en: THE SCRAP OF LANGUAGE: an uninflected word is treated as a loose piece, and one such piece can carry negation.
branches.cn: 语言碎片：不变化的词被看作散件，而这样一个散件就能承担否定。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the speck becomes the smallest possible share of a quality such as truth.
branches.cn: 尺度：微粒成为真这类品质的最小可能份额。

branches.en: THE ATOM OF THOUGHT: an argument is ground down to particles and rebuilt.
branches.cn: 思想之原子：一套论证被磨成颗粒，再由颗粒重建。

intro.en: Particle is built from a Latin root for part and a diminutive suffix, and that root also supplies several abstract English words.
intro.cn: particle 由表示「部分」的拉丁词根加指小后缀构成，这个词根还供给若干抽象英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars, partis yields part, particle, partial, particular and portion; the diminutive marker is what makes particle mean a small piece rather than a share.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「部分」衍生 part、particle、partial、particular 与 portion；指小标记正是让 particle 表示小片而非份额的关键。

items.example: The root states that something is only a piece of a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根说明某物只是整体的一块。

items.example: The suffix shrinks the base noun without changing its kind.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把基础名词缩小，却不改变它的类别。

items.example: A crumb is a little part of the loaf.
items.exampleCN: 一块碎屑就是面包的一小部分。

items.example: The particle was too small to see.
items.exampleCN: 这个微粒小到看不见。

items.example: A partial answer leaves the rest unexplained.
items.exampleCN: 部分回答把其余部分留在未解释中。

items.example: Each particular case needs its own file.
items.exampleCN: 每一个具体个案都需要自己的档案。

items.meaningCN: 以分离颗粒形式存在的
items.example: Particulate matter hangs in the air.
items.exampleCN: 颗粒物悬浮在空气中。

definition_zh: 亚原子的；比原子更小的；原子内部层次的
definition_en: smaller than an atom, or existing within the internal structure of an atom
core_image: 一枚完整的果子被剖开，里面还嵌着更小的核，核里又有更小的点
scene: 对撞机里两束粒子迎面撞上，探测器亮起成片信号。The collision revealed a subatomic structure that no microscope could show.
sceneCN: 这里 subatomic 指「比原子更小、位于原子内部层次」（第 1 个义项：尺度小于原子的）；句意：这次碰撞揭示出一种任何显微镜都显示不出的亚原子结构。图中可辨识物件：对撞管道、探测层、信号点、控制台。

derivatives.zh: 亚核的；比原子核更小的
亚分子的；比分子更小的

senses.title: Smaller than an atom
senses.definition: of a size below that of an atom, too small to be described as an ordinary chemical unit
senses.definitionCN: 尺寸小于原子，小到不能当作普通化学单元来描述
senses.example: The force acts only over subatomic distances.
senses.exampleCN: 这种力只在亚原子距离内起作用。
senses.why: The Latin prefix means 'under' and the second half means 'atom', so the word literally places something beneath the atomic level.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀意为「在下」，后半意为「原子」，因此这个词字面上就是把某物放到原子层次之下。

senses.title: A particle inside the atom
senses.definition: describing a particle that is a constituent of the atom, such as an electron, a proton or a neutron
senses.definitionCN: 描述构成原子的粒子，如电子、质子或中子
senses.example: Electrons are the lightest subatomic particles in ordinary matter.
senses.exampleCN: 电子是普通物质里最轻的亚原子粒子。
senses.why: Once the atom stopped being indivisible, the pieces inside it needed a name, and 'below the atom' supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 原子不再不可分之后，里面的碎块需要一个名字，「在原子之下」正好补上。

senses.title: The branch that studies those pieces
senses.definition: the field of physics concerned with particles and forces inside the atom
senses.definitionCN: 研究原子内部粒子与力的物理学分支
senses.example: Subatomic physics grew out of radioactivity research.
senses.exampleCN: 亚原子物理学从放射性的研究中成长起来。
senses.why: The adjective simply modifies the name of the discipline, so the subject is called by the scale it works at.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是修饰学科名，于是这门学科就以它工作的尺度来称呼。

senses.title: The layered structure of the atom
senses.definition: the internal arrangement of a nucleus surrounded by electrons, considered as a structure rather than a single object
senses.definitionCN: 由原子核与外围电子构成的内部排列，被当作一种结构而非单一物体
senses.example: Textbooks draw the subatomic structure as a dense centre and a cloud of charge.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把亚原子结构画成致密的中心与一团电荷云。
senses.why: The word can describe the whole internal architecture, not just a single particle, because the prefix marks a level rather than an item.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述整个内部构造，而不只是单个粒子，因为前缀标的是一个层次而非一件东西。

senses.title: Forces that act at that depth
senses.titleCN: 在那一深度起作用的力
senses.definition: the strong and weak interactions, which operate only across subatomic ranges
senses.definitionCN: 强相互作用与弱相互作用，它们只在亚原子范围内起作用
senses.example: The strong force holds the nucleus together at subatomic range.
senses.exampleCN: 强力在亚原子范围内把原子核维系在一起。
senses.why: Because these forces die out long before ordinary distances, they are named by the scale at which they exist.
senses.whyCN: 这些力在普通距离之前早已消失，因此以它们存在的那一尺度来命名。

senses.title: Debris from a collision
senses.definition: the fragments produced when accelerated particles strike a target and break it apart
senses.definitionCN: 被加速的粒子撞击靶体、将其打散时产生的碎片
senses.example: The detector counted every subatomic fragment from the impact.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器记下了撞击产生的每一块亚原子碎片。
senses.why: A collision exposes the interior by breaking it, so what flies out is literally subatomic debris.
senses.whyCN: 碰撞靠打碎来暴露内部，因此飞出的东西字面上就是亚原子碎片。

senses.title: Resolution below the atomic scale
senses.titleCN: 低于原子尺度的分辨能力
senses.definition: a level of detail in imaging or measurement that reaches inside the atom
senses.definitionCN: 成像或测量中深入到原子内部的细节水平
senses.example: The new instrument reaches subatomic resolution without destroying the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 新仪器能在不破坏样品的情况下达到亚原子分辨率。
senses.why: The same adjective describes how finely a tool can see, because seeing below the atom is the same achievement as being below it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词也描述工具能看多细，因为看见原子之下与处在原子之下是同一件事的两面。

senses.title: Abstract: analysed to the smallest parts
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：分析到最小的组成部分
senses.definition: taken apart into components finer than any ordinary division
senses.definitionCN: 被拆解成比任何常规划分都更细的组成部分
senses.example: The committee went subatomic on a budget that needed only a glance.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把一份只需扫一眼的预算拆到了最小的项目。
senses.why: The physical scale became a metaphor for excessive detail, since going below the atom means going past every visible division.
senses.whyCN: 物理尺度变成了「细得过分」的比喻，因为到原子之下就意味着越过了所有可见的划分。

intro.en: Subatomic is a modern English compound: Latin sub 'under' plus atomic, which comes from Greek atomos 'uncuttable'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subatomic 是近代英语复合词：拉丁前缀「在下」加 atomic，而 atomic 出自希腊语「不可切分的」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sub is a Latin preposition and prefix meaning 'under, below', and it regularly forms words of a lower rank or layer.
items.cn: sub 是拉丁介词与介词性前缀，意为「在下、低于」，常构成表示较低等级或层次的词。

items.en: Atomos meant 'uncuttable', built from the negative prefix a- and temnein 'to cut'. Ancient thinkers used it for the smallest indivisible body.
items.cn: atomos 意为「不可切分的」，由否定前缀加「切」构成。古代思想家以此指最小不可分的物体。

items.en: When chemistry showed that the atom has parts, English kept the old name for the whole and needed a new word for what lies beneath.
items.cn: 化学证明原子有内部结构之后，英语保留旧名指整体，又需要新词指它下面的东西。

items.en: Subatomic entered technical writing as electrons, protons and neutrons were identified, and it spread to forces, structure and resolution.
items.cn: 随着电子、质子与中子被辨认，这个词进入技术写作，并扩展到力、结构与分辨率。

items.en: The first recorded uses for each technical phrase are approximate; the two source words are old and well attested.
items.cn: 各技术短语的最早书证年代为约数；两个来源词都古老且有充分记录。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the atom-root or from the same under-prefix; group two holds scale words that are often used interchangeably with it.
note.cn: 第一组是由「原子」词根或同一「在下」前缀构成的词；第二组是常与它互换使用的尺度词。

entries.definition: Relating to an atom as a whole, as in atomic number or atomic energy; it stops at the atom, while subatomic goes inside.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个原子的，如原子序数或原子能；它止于原子，而这个词进入原子内部。

entries.definition: The whole chemical unit, once thought indivisible; the adjective under discussion names what lies beneath this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的化学单元，曾被认为不可分；所讨论的形容词正指这个名词之下的层次。

entries.definition: Under water, from the same Latin 'under' plus a word for water; the prefix matches but the base has nothing to do with atoms.
entries.definitionCN: 水下的，由同一个拉丁「在下」加表示水的词构成；前缀相同，词基却与原子无关。

entries.definition: Below the molecular level; a sister formation that applies the same prefix to a larger unit.
entries.definitionCN: 低于分子层次；用同一前缀加在更大的单位上构成的姊妹词。

entries.definition: Too small to be seen with the naked eye, but still far larger than the atomic scale.
entries.definitionCN: 小到肉眼看不见，但仍远大于原子尺度。

entries.definition: Relating to molecules, the level above atoms; subatomic is the level below.
entries.definitionCN: 指分子的，位于原子之上；这个词则指原子之下的层次。

entries.definition: Used for a particle believed to have no internal parts; it answers a different question from the size word.
entries.definitionCN: 用于被认为没有内部结构的粒子；它回答的是另一个问题，而非尺寸问题。

entries.definition: A mathematical word for a quantity approaching zero; it measures size in theory, not structure in matter.
entries.definitionCN: 数学上指趋近于零的量；它衡量理论上的大小，而非物质的内部结构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin sub 'under' plus atomic: beneath the atom.
normal.cn: 拉丁「在下」加原子的：原子之下。

normal.en: The family runs subatomic, subatomically, subnuclear, submolecular.
normal.cn: 同族词包括亚原子的、亚原子地、亚核的、亚分子的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: subatomic particle, subatomic level, subatomic structure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出尺度：亚原子粒子、亚原子层次、亚原子结构。

normal.en: The atom itself is named from Greek 'uncuttable', so the word is a joke one level down: the uncuttable has inside parts.
normal.cn: 原子本名出自希腊语「不可切分」，于是这个词在下一层开了个玩笑：不可切分的东西内部还有零件。

normal.en: Electron, proton and neutron are the standard subatomic particles.
normal.cn: 电子、质子与中子是标准的亚原子粒子。

abstract.en: Picture a fruit cut open to show a stone, and the stone cut again to show a smaller core.
abstract.cn: 想象果子剖开露出核，核再剖开又露出更小的芯。

abstract.en: Picture a map that zooms past every street until only dots of ink remain.
abstract.cn: 想象地图不断放大，越过所有街道，最后只剩墨点。

abstract.en: Picture a budget examined so closely that each pencil is listed separately.
abstract.cn: 想象预算被细看到连每一支铅笔都单列一行。

examples.en: The nucleus is held together by forces on the subatomic scale.
examples.cn: 原子核由亚原子尺度上的力维系在一起。

examples.en: Subatomic particles were once thought to be only three kinds.
examples.cn: 亚原子粒子曾被认为只有三种。

examples.en: The review examined the plan at a subatomic level of detail.
examples.cn: 这次评审以极其细微的程度检查了该计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub（下面）+ atomic（原子）」——原子下面那一层，就是亚原子

root: 拉丁 sub「在下」+ atomic（希腊 atomos「不可切分的」= 否定前缀 a- + temnein「切」）。英语 subatomic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight uses descend one level: scale below the atom, the parts inside it, the discipline, the internal architecture, the forces at that range, collision debris, imaging detail, and finally a metaphor for analysis that goes too deep.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个用法都在下一层展开：小于原子的尺度、内部的零件、这门学科、内部构造、那一范围里的力、碰撞碎片、成像细节，最后是「分析得过细」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one level beneath the atom, where the uncuttable turns out to have parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：原子下面的一层，在那里「不可切分之物」露出了零件。

branches.en: THE LEVEL AND ITS TENANTS: being smaller than an atom and being one of its pieces are the same descent seen twice.
branches.cn: 层次与住户：小于原子与作为原子的零件，是同一次下潜的两种看法。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the scale becomes the name of the field that works there.
branches.cn: 学科：这一尺度成了在那里工作的领域的名字。

branches.en: THE ARCHITECTURE: a centre, a cloud and the forces that hold the arrangement are all read at this depth.
branches.cn: 构造：中心、云团以及维系排列的力，都在这一深度被读出。

branches.en: THE TOOLS: breaking matter apart and seeing inside it are two ways of reaching the same layer.
branches.cn: 工具：打散物质与看见内部，是抵达同一层次的两种办法。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: go below every visible division and analysis becomes absurdly fine.
branches.cn: 比喻：越过所有可见划分之后，分析就细得荒唐。

intro.en: Subatomic is a hybrid: a Latin prefix joined to an adjective whose root is Greek, a common pattern in scientific English.
intro.cn: subatomic 是混合造词：拉丁前缀接在一个希腊词根的形容词上，这是科学英语里常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub supplies several English prefixes, and atomic comes through Latin atomus from Greek atomos; the Latin noun atomus is a direct borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sub 供给若干英语前缀，atomic 则经拉丁 atomus 出自希腊 atomos；拉丁名词 atomus 是直接借词。

items.example: The prefix places one thing beneath another.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把一物置于另一物之下。

items.example: The negative prefix denies the action of the root.
items.exampleCN: 这个否定前缀否定了词根所表示的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the cutting that the negative prefix denies.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供被否定前缀否掉的那个「切」。

items.example: The ancient atom was named for not being cuttable.
items.exampleCN: 古代的原子因不可切分而得名。

items.example: Atomic mass is measured in standard units.
items.exampleCN: 原子质量以标准单位计量。

items.example: Subatomic events last a tiny fraction of a second.
items.exampleCN: 亚原子事件只持续极短的一瞬。

items.example: Subnuclear forces bind quarks.
items.exampleCN: 亚核力把夸克束缚在一起。

items.example: Submolecular imaging shows single bonds.
items.exampleCN: 亚分子成像能显示单根化学键。

definition_zh: 量子；能量或物质的最小不连续单位；定量；份额
definition_en: the smallest discrete amount of a physical quantity, or a fixed share of something
core_image: 水管里流出的水看起来连续，换成极小的量杯量，却总是一格一格地落下
scene: 炉壁烧到发红时，放出的能量并非连续不断。Planck found that energy leaves a hot body in one quantum at a time.
sceneCN: 这里 quantum 指「能量不可再分的最小一份」（第 1 个义项：某个物理量的最小不连续单位）；句意：普朗克发现能量从炽热物体离开时，一次只放出一个量子。图中可辨识物件：炉壁、分格的能量块、温度计、记录纸。

pos.zh: 量子；定量（可数，复数形式为拉丁式）
量子的（作定语，如量子力学）

derivatives.zh: 使量子化；按离散单位处理

senses.title: The smallest discrete packet of energy
senses.titleCN: 能量不可再分的最小一份
senses.definition: the least amount of energy that can be emitted, absorbed or exchanged in a single event
senses.definitionCN: 在一次事件中被放出、吸收或交换的最小能量
senses.example: A photon carries one quantum of light energy.
senses.exampleCN: 一个光子携带一份光能量子。
senses.why: Latin quantum means 'how much', and physics narrowed that question to the smallest amount that can be counted at all.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义是「多少」，物理学把这个问法收窄成「能被计数的最小一份」。

senses.title: One packet of light
senses.definition: a single unit of electromagnetic energy, later called a photon
senses.definitionCN: 电磁能量的单一单位，后来称为光子
senses.example: Einstein treated each light quantum as a separate particle.
senses.exampleCN: 爱因斯坦把每一份光量子当作独立的粒子。
senses.why: Light was the first quantity found to come in packets, so the general unit became the everyday name for a light packet.
senses.whyCN: 光是最早被发现按份出现的量，于是这个通用单位成了光的一份的日常称呼。

senses.title: The plural units counted in theory
senses.titleCN: 理论中计数的复数单位
senses.definition: the countable units into which a physical quantity is divided, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某个物理量被分成的可数单位，通常用复数
senses.example: The theory adds up the contributions of many quanta.
senses.exampleCN: 这套理论把许多量子的贡献累加起来。
senses.why: Once a thing arrives in packets, calculations count packets, so the plural became the working noun of the theory.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物按份到来，计算就要清点份数，于是复数成了理论的常用名词。

senses.title: The adjective of the quantum world
senses.definition: used before another noun to mark a field, state or rule that belongs to quantum theory
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，标出属于量子理论的领域、状态或规则
senses.example: Quantum theory replaced the smooth classical picture.
senses.exampleCN: 量子理论取代了平滑的经典图景。
senses.why: English routinely turns a key noun into a modifier, so quantum now labels whole fields without changing its form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把关键名词直接当定语，因此这个词不改词形就能标记整个领域。

senses.title: An abrupt jump between atomic states
senses.titleCN: 原子状态之间的突然跳变
senses.definition: the discontinuous change of an electron from one energy level to another
senses.definitionCN: 电子从一个能级到另一个能级的不连续变化
senses.example: The electron makes a quantum jump and emits a single photon.
senses.exampleCN: 电子发生一次量子跃迁，并放出一个光子。
senses.why: Because energy levels are discrete, a change between them cannot be gradual; it is a jump of one quantum.
senses.whyCN: 能级是分立的，因此能级之间的变化不可能渐变，只能是一份量子的跳跃。

senses.title: A sudden large advance in ordinary life
senses.titleCN: 日常语境里的突然大跨越
senses.definition: a dramatic and abrupt improvement or change, usually in the phrase quantum leap
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧性且突然的改进或变化，通常用于「量子跃迁」这一短语
senses.example: The new vaccine was a quantum leap in prevention.
senses.exampleCN: 新疫苗在预防上是巨大的一步。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the smallest possible jump in physics and reverses its scale, turning it into the biggest step imaginable.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了物理上最小的一跳，却把尺度反过来，变成想象中最大的一步。

senses.title: The adjective of quantum computing
senses.definition: used of information technology that exploits superposition or entanglement, as in quantum computing
senses.definitionCN: 用于利用叠加或纠缠的信息技术，如量子计算
senses.example: The laboratory built a quantum processor with a hundred units.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室造出一台拥有一百个单元的量子处理器。
senses.why: The same modifier extends to any technology built on discrete quantum states, so computing joined the family.
senses.whyCN: 同一个定语扩展到任何建立在分立量子态上的技术，于是计算也加入了这个家族。

senses.title: A required share or amount
senses.definition: a fixed amount of something required or allotted, as in a quantum of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 所需或被分配的固定分量，如「一份证据」
senses.example: The claim needs a quantum of proof before it can be heard.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法在获准陈述之前需要一定分量的证据。
senses.why: The legal and formal sense keeps the original 'how much': a case needs a measurable minimum, not a vague impression.
senses.whyCN: 法律与正式用法保留了原本的「多少」：一个案子需要可量的最低分量，而不是模糊印象。

intro.en: Quantum is a Latin neuter form meaning 'how much', adopted by physics in 1900 for the smallest indivisible amount of energy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: quantum 是拉丁语中性形式，意为「多少」；物理学在 1900 年用它指能量不可再分的最小一份。年代均为约数。

items.en: Quantus was the interrogative and relative adjective 'how great, how much', parallel to tantus 'so great' and qualis 'of what kind'.
items.cn: quantus 是疑问与关系形容词「多大、多少」，与「这么大」和「何种」两个词平行。

items.en: The neuter singular quantum meant 'how much', and in legal and philosophical writing it named a fixed quantity or share.
items.cn: 中性单数 quantum 意为「多少」，在法律与哲学写作中指固定的量或份额。

items.en: Planck proposed that energy is exchanged in fixed packets, and he called each packet an energy quantum, keeping the Latin question word.
items.cn: 普朗克提出能量按固定小包交换，并把每一包称为能量子，沿用了这个拉丁疑问词。

items.en: Einstein extended the idea to light, speaking of light quanta; the name photon came later, but the quantum stayed.
items.cn: 爱因斯坦把这一想法扩展到光，说到光量子；光子的名字出现得更晚，量子却留了下来。

items.en: The phrase for an electron's discontinuous change passed into general speech in the twentieth century as a figure for any sudden advance.
items.cn: 描述电子不连续变化的短语在二十世纪进入日常语言，成为任何突然进步的比喻。

items.en: The exact first written uses for the figurative and computing senses are approximate; the Latin source and the physics coinage are well dated.
items.cn: 比喻义与计算义的最早书面用例年代为约数；拉丁来源与物理学造词的年代都有明确记录。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same how-much root; group two holds amount words that overlap with quantum outside physics.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「多少」词根的词；第二组是物理学之外与 quantum 重叠的数量词。

entries.definition: From Latin quantitas, built on quantus: how much there is of something, measured without the idea of a smallest packet.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语，构于「多少」之上：某物有多少，不含「最小一份」的意思。

entries.definition: From Latin quota pars 'how great a part': an allotted share, from the same family of quantity words.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「多大的一份」：分配到的份额，同属数量词族。

entries.definition: From Latin quorum 'of whom', the opening word of a commission's formula: the minimum number of members needed, not a quantum.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「其中之人的」，是委任套语的开头：指所需的最低人数，并非量子。

entries.definition: Of uncertain origin and no connection with quantus: a state of puzzled doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 来源不确定，与「多少」无关：指困惑两难的处境。

entries.definition: An ordinary word for a small wrapped portion; it conveys the 'arrives in portions' idea without the physics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常指一小包东西；能传达「按份到来」的意思，但不含物理含义。

entries.definition: A general word for one countable item or standard measure; quantum is a unit fixed by nature, not by convention.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指一个可数项或标准计量；量子是由自然固定而非由人约定的单位。

entries.definition: The modern name for a light quantum; every photon is a quantum, but not every quantum is a photon.
entries.definitionCN: 光量子的现代名称；每个光子都是量子，但并非每个量子都是光子。

entries.definition: A general word for how much of something exists, with no suggestion of discreteness.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某物有多少，不含分立性的暗示。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin quantum 'how much': physics asks how much, and finds a smallest answer.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「多少」：物理学问「多少」，却找到一个最小的答案。

normal.en: The family runs quantum, quanta, quantize, quantization, quantal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括量子、量子（复数）、使量子化、量子化、分立的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: quantum of energy, light quantum, quantum leap.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：能量子、光量子、量子跃迁。

normal.en: The same root appears in quantity and quota, both about measuring how much.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在数量与配额里，都与衡量多少有关。

normal.en: Outside physics the phrase quantum leap means a huge jump, even though a real quantum jump is the smallest possible one.
normal.cn: 物理学之外，「量子跃迁」指巨大跨越，而真正的量子跃迁恰恰是最小的一跳。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose steps are so small that they look like a slope from far away.
abstract.cn: 想象一级级极小的台阶，远看却像一道斜坡。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that can only be switched to fixed brightness levels, never dimmed smoothly.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只能调到固定的几档亮度，无法平滑变暗。

abstract.en: Picture a cash machine that pays only in whole coins, never in fractions.
abstract.cn: 想象取款机只付整枚硬币，从不付零头。

examples.en: Energy is absorbed in quanta, not in a smooth stream.
examples.cn: 能量按量子被吸收，而不是连续不断地流入。

examples.en: Each quantum of light carries a fixed amount of energy.
examples.cn: 每一份光量子都携带固定的能量。

examples.en: The discovery was a quantum leap for the whole field.
examples.cn: 这一发现对整个领域是巨大的一步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「quant（量）+ um」——量到不能再分的那一格，就是量子

root: 拉丁 quantum「多少」，为 quantus「多大」的中性形式；同族含 quantity、quota。英语 quantum。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the smallest packet of energy, pass through the light packet, the plural units and the attributive label, then to an electron's jump, its figurative reversal, quantum computing and finally a required share.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最小的一份能量开始，经过光的一份、复数的单位与定语用法，再到电子的一跳、被反过来用的比喻、量子计算，最后是必需的份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quantity that looks continuous from afar but arrives in indivisible steps when measured closely.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个远看连续的量，凑近测量时却按不可分的台阶到来。

branches.en: THE PACKET: energy and light are the same discovery seen twice, since light was the first quantity found in packets.
branches.cn: 小包：能量与光是同一发现的两面，因为光是最早被发现按包出现的量。

branches.en: THE COUNT: once things arrive in packets, theory counts packets and the plural becomes a working noun.
branches.cn: 计数：一旦事物按包到来，理论就清点包数，复数便成了常用名词。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the noun turns into a modifier and marks whole fields, from theory to computing.
branches.cn: 标签：名词转成定语，标记整个领域，从理论到计算。

branches.en: THE JUMP: discreteness forces an abrupt change, and everyday speech borrows it while reversing its size.
branches.cn: 跳跃：分立性迫使变化突然发生，日常语言借走它，却把大小反过来。

branches.en: THE SHARE: law and formal prose keep the original question and ask for a measurable minimum.
branches.cn: 份额：法律与正式文章保留原本的「多少」，要求一个可量的最低分量。

intro.en: Quantum is a Latin pronominal adjective turned noun, and its root family is small but busy in English.
intro.cn: quantum 是拉丁代词性形容词转成的名词，它的词根词族不大，却在英语里很活跃。

latinIntro.en: Latin quantus and quantum yield quantity, quantify, quantitative and quota in English; the ending -um marks the neuter form used as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 quantus 与 quantum 在英语里衍生出数量、量化、定量的与配额；-um 结尾标出用作名词的中性形式。

items.example: The adjective asks for a measure of size.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词问的是大小或分量。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.structure: quantum (neuter of quantus, used as a noun)
items.example: The court asked for a quantum of proof.
items.exampleCN: 法庭要求一定分量的证据。

items.example: The theory sums over many quanta.
items.exampleCN: 理论对许多量子求和。

items.example: Engineers quantize the signal before storing it.
items.exampleCN: 工程师在存储前先把信号量化。

items.example: Quantization removes the smooth continuum.
items.exampleCN: 量化去掉了平滑的连续体。

items.example: The quantity was measured twice.
items.exampleCN: 这个数量被测量了两次。

items.example: Each port received a fixed quota.
items.exampleCN: 每个港口分到固定的配额。

latinEntries.structure: quantum (neuter singular of quantus, used as a noun)

definition_zh: 量子力学；描述原子与亚原子尺度物质行为的物理学理论
definition_en: the branch of physics that describes matter and energy at atomic and subatomic scales using discrete states and probabilities
core_image: 一粒电子没有确定的轨道，只有一团浓淡不一的云，云越浓的地方越可能找到它
scene: 黑板上写满波函数与概率，学生算出一个电子最可能出现的位置。Quantum mechanics predicts where the electron will probably be found.
sceneCN: 这里 quantum mechanics 指「描述原子尺度物质行为的理论」（第 1 个义项：以分立状态与概率描述微观粒子的物理学框架）；句意：量子力学预测这个电子最可能出现在哪里。图中可辨识物件：黑板、波函数曲线、概率云、计算尺。

pos.zh: 量子力学（不可数，作主语时视为单数）

derivatives.zh: 矩阵力学（量子力学的一种表述）
波动力学（量子力学的另一种表述）

senses.title: The theory of matter at atomic scale
senses.definition: the physical framework that describes how matter and energy behave at atomic and subatomic scales
senses.definitionCN: 描述物质与能量在原子及亚原子尺度上如何行为的物理框架
senses.example: Quantum mechanics explains why atoms emit light at fixed colours.
senses.exampleCN: 量子力学解释了原子为何只发出固定颜色的光。
senses.why: Mechanics names the study of motion, and quantum names the discrete units, so the phrase is 'the mechanics of discrete amounts'.
senses.whyCN: 力学是研究运动的学问，量子指分立单位，因此这个短语就是「分立之量的力学」。

senses.title: The university subject
senses.definition: the course or textbook subject in which the theory is taught
senses.definitionCN: 讲授这套理论的课程或教科书科目
senses.example: She took quantum mechanics in her second year.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第二年修了量子力学。
senses.why: Any named theory becomes a teachable subject, so the phrase also names the timetable slot rather than the physics itself.
senses.whyCN: 任何有名字的理论都会成为可教的科目，因此这个短语也指课程表上的那一格，而非物理本身。

senses.title: The mathematical formalism
senses.definition: the wavefunctions, operators and state spaces used to calculate quantum behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 用来计算量子行为的波函数、算符与状态空间
senses.example: The formalism of quantum mechanics turns observations into operators.
senses.exampleCN: 量子力学的形式体系把观测量变成算符。
senses.why: To be useful, the theory must be written in mathematics, and that machinery is often called by the theory's name.
senses.whyCN: 理论要有用就得写成数学，而这套机器常被直接用理论之名来称呼。

senses.title: Probabilistic prediction
senses.definition: the rule that only the likelihood of a result can be predicted, not the result itself
senses.definitionCN: 只能预测结果的概率、不能预测结果本身的规则
senses.example: Quantum mechanics gives odds, not a single certain path.
senses.exampleCN: 量子力学给出的是几率，而不是唯一确定的路径。
senses.why: The theory's deepest break with classical physics is that it replaces certainty with probability, and that feature is named after it.
senses.whyCN: 这套理论与经典物理最深的决裂，是用概率取代确定性，这一特征便以它命名。

senses.title: The tool for chemistry and materials
senses.titleCN: 用于化学与材料学的工具
senses.definition: the applied use of the theory to explain bonds, spectra and the properties of solids
senses.definitionCN: 把理论用于解释化学键、光谱与固体性质
senses.example: Quantum mechanics now guides the design of new catalysts.
senses.exampleCN: 量子力学如今指导新催化剂的设计。
senses.why: Once the equations could be solved by computer, the theory became an everyday tool in neighbouring sciences.
senses.whyCN: 方程能由计算机求解之后，这套理论就成了邻近学科的日常工具。

senses.title: The classical limit
senses.titleCN: 经典极限：大尺度下退回经典物理
senses.definition: the way quantum rules approach ordinary classical behaviour when objects become large or warm
senses.definitionCN: 当物体变大或变热时，量子规则趋近普通经典行为的方式
senses.example: The correspondence principle shows how quantum mechanics becomes classical mechanics.
senses.exampleCN: 对应原理显示量子力学如何变为经典力学。
senses.why: A theory that governs atoms must still explain why the world looks ordinary, so its own limit became one of its named topics.
senses.whyCN: 管着原子的理论仍须解释世界为何看起来平常，因此它自身的极限成了它的一个专题。

senses.title: Competing interpretations
senses.definition: the rival accounts, such as the Copenhagen view or many worlds, of what the mathematics means
senses.definitionCN: 关于这套数学究竟意味着什么的不同说法，如哥本哈根解释或多世界解释
senses.example: The two camps argue about the interpretation of quantum mechanics, not its predictions.
senses.exampleCN: 两派争论的是量子力学的解释，而不是它的预测。
senses.why: The equations work while their meaning is disputed, so 'interpretation of quantum mechanics' became a field of its own.
senses.whyCN: 方程有效，含义却有争议，于是「量子力学的解释」自成一门学问。

senses.title: The relativistic extension
senses.definition: the version of the theory adjusted for speeds near that of light, leading to quantum field theory
senses.definitionCN: 为接近光速的情况作出调整的版本，进而通向量子场论
senses.example: Relativistic quantum mechanics was needed before antimatter could be predicted.
senses.exampleCN: 必须先有相对论性量子力学，才可能预测反物质。
senses.why: The original theory assumed slow motion, so joining it to relativity became a distinct and named extension.
senses.whyCN: 最初的理论假定运动缓慢，因此把它与相对论结合成一个有专门名称的推广。

intro.en: Quantum mechanics joins Latin quantum 'how much' to mechanics, which comes through Latin mechanica from Greek mēkhanē 'machine, device'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: quantum mechanics 把拉丁语「多少」接到 mechanics 上，而 mechanics 经拉丁 mechanica 出自希腊语「机械、装置」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mēkhanē meant 'a machine, a contrivance, a device for lifting', and mēkhanikos described what belongs to machines.
items.cn: mēkhanē 意为「机械、装置、用来起吊的工具」，mēkhanikos 描述与机械有关之物。

items.en: Latin borrowed mechanica as the name of the science of machines and motion, and English mechanics came through that route.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 mechanica 作为机械与运动之学的名称，英语的 mechanics 经此路径而来。

items.en: Quantum 'how much' entered physics in 1900 as the name of the smallest energy packet, and the adjective sense followed.
items.cn: 表示「多少」的 quantum 在 1900 年作为最小能量包之名进入物理学，其定语用法随后出现。

items.en: In the mid-1920s two formulations, matrix mechanics and wave mechanics, were shown to be one theory, and the joint name quantum mechanics took hold.
items.cn: 二十世纪二十年代中期，矩阵力学与波动力学两种表述被证明是同一理论，「量子力学」这个合名便固定下来。

items.en: Relativistic quantum mechanics and quantum field theory extended the name, while the classical limit kept it tied to ordinary mechanics.
items.cn: 相对论性量子力学与量子场论扩展了这个名称，而经典极限又把它与普通力学连在一起。

items.en: The first written use of the exact English phrase is approximate; both source words are fully attested.
items.cn: 这个英语短语最早的书证年代为约数；两个来源词都有完整记录。

note.en: Group one holds mechanics words built on the same Greek machine-root; group two holds the neighbouring quantum theories it is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「机械」词根的力学词；第二组是常与它混淆的邻近量子理论。

entries.definition: The older mechanics of Newton, with definite positions and speeds; it is the limit that quantum mechanics must reproduce.
entries.definitionCN: 牛顿的旧力学，位置与速度皆确定；它是量子力学必须重现的极限。

entries.definition: From the same machine-root but with a result suffix: the working parts of a device or a process, not a mathematical theory.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「机械」词根，但带结果后缀：指装置或过程的运作部件，而非数学理论。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines, or an adjective meaning mechanical; the plural form alone became the science.
entries.definitionCN: 指修机器的人，或作形容词表示机械的；单是复数形式才成为学科名。

entries.definition: A broader label for the whole framework of discrete physics, of which quantum mechanics is the core calculational part.
entries.definitionCN: 对整个分立物理框架的更宽泛称呼，量子力学是其中核心的计算部分。

entries.definition: The whole branch of physics dealing with quantum effects; quantum mechanics is its main theoretical engine.
entries.definitionCN: 研究量子效应的整个物理学分支；量子力学是其主要理论引擎。

entries.definition: The wave-equation version of quantum mechanics; it is a form of the theory, not a rival to it.
entries.definitionCN: 量子力学的波动方程版本；它是该理论的一种形式，并非其对手。

entries.definition: The framework that combines quantum mechanics with fields and relativity, needed for particles being created and destroyed.
entries.definitionCN: 把量子力学与场、相对论结合起来的框架，用于处理粒子的产生与湮灭。

entries.definition: The mechanics of many particles using ordinary statistics; its probability comes from ignorance, not from nature.
entries.definitionCN: 用普通统计处理大量粒子的力学；其概率来自无知，而非自然本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: quantum 'how much' plus mechanics 'the study of machines and motion': the mechanics of discrete amounts.
normal.cn: 「多少」加「机械与运动之学」：分立之量的力学。

normal.en: The family runs quantum mechanics, quantum-mechanical, matrix mechanics, wave mechanics.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括量子力学、量子力学的、矩阵力学、波动力学。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: foundations of quantum mechanics, laws of quantum mechanics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：量子力学基础、量子力学定律。

normal.en: Mechanics itself comes from the Greek word for a machine, so the name literally means machine science.
normal.cn: 力学一词本身出自希腊语的「机械」，因此这个名字字面上就是机械之学。

normal.en: The theory's signature is probability: it predicts odds, not single paths.
normal.cn: 这套理论的标志是概率：它预测几率，而非唯一路径。

abstract.en: Picture an electron as a cloud of guesses, thick where the answer is likely.
abstract.cn: 想象电子是一团猜测之云，答案可能的地方云更浓。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that can only be set to fixed gears, never to a smooth in-between speed.
abstract.cn: 想象一台只能挂固定档位、无法无级变速的机器。

abstract.en: Picture a rule book that gives odds for every move instead of one prescribed move.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则书，为每一步给出几率，而不是规定唯一步法。

examples.en: Quantum mechanics was built to explain the stable colours of heated atoms.
examples.cn: 量子力学是为了解释受热原子稳定的颜色而建立的。

examples.en: The chemistry course assumes no prior study of quantum mechanics.
examples.cn: 这门化学课假定学生此前没有学过量子力学。

examples.en: Engineers use quantum mechanics to predict how a new material will conduct.
examples.cn: 工程师用量子力学预测新材料的导电方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「quantum（量子）+ mechanics（力学）」——管量子那一层的力学，就是量子力学

root: quantum（拉丁「多少」，量子）+ mechanics（拉丁 mechanica，出自希腊 mēkhanē「机械、装置」）。英语 quantum mechanics。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the theory itself to its classroom form, its mathematics, its probability rule, its use in chemistry, its classical limit, its disputed interpretations and its relativistic extension.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从理论本身走到课堂形态、数学形式、概率规则、化学应用、经典极限、有争议的解释，最后是相对论性推广。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloud of probability instead of a fixed orbit, with the densest part marking the likely place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条固定轨道被一团概率云取代，最浓处标出可能出现的位置。

branches.en: THEORY AND TIMETABLE: a framework of physics and a slot in the curriculum are the same name used at two removes.
branches.cn: 理论与课表：物理框架与课程表上的一格，是同一个名字隔了一层的两种用法。

branches.en: THE MACHINERY: wavefunctions and operators are the working parts that make the theory calculable.
branches.cn: 机器：波函数与算符是使理论可计算的运作部件。

branches.en: THE ODDS: certainty is replaced by likelihood, the sharpest break with the older mechanics.
branches.cn: 几率：确定性被可能性取代，这是与旧力学最锋利的决裂。

branches.en: THE TWO DIRECTIONS: the theory reaches into chemistry and materials, and must also explain how ordinary mechanics returns at large scales.
branches.cn: 两个方向：理论伸进化学与材料，也须解释普通力学如何在大尺度上回归。

branches.en: THE UNFINISHED EDGE: meaning is still argued, and the theory must be joined to relativity.
branches.cn: 未完成的边缘：含义仍有争论，理论还须与相对论结合。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin quantity word to a Greek-derived name for the science of machines, so its two halves have separate histories.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的数量词接到一个源自希腊的机械之学名称上，两半各自有独立的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin quantum supplies the first half; Latin mechanica, borrowed from Greek, supplies the second and also yields machine, mechanism and mechanic.
latinIntro.cn: 前半由拉丁 quantum 提供；后半来自借入拉丁语的 mechanica，并衍生出 machine、mechanism、mechanic。

items.example: The first word marks the discrete scale.
items.exampleCN: 第一个词标出分立的尺度。

items.example: The root names any built device for doing work.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指任何为做功而造的装置。

items.meaning: the science of machines and motion
items.example: Medieval writers divided mechanics from astronomy.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪作者把机械学与天文学分开。

items.meaning: the study of motion and forces
items.example: Mechanics predicts where a falling stone lands.
items.exampleCN: 力学预测落石落在何处。

items.example: Quantum mechanics governs the atom's energy levels.
items.exampleCN: 量子力学支配原子的能级。

items.example: The effect is purely quantum-mechanical.
items.exampleCN: 这一效应纯粹属于量子力学。

items.meaning: the working parts of a device
items.example: The clock's mechanism was open to view.
items.exampleCN: 钟的运作机构敞开可见。

items.example: The machine lifted the stone by leverage.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器靠杠杆抬起石头。

latinEntries.structure: quantum (neuter of quantus, used as a noun)
