machina, machinae (f., first declension, from Greek mēkhanē)

definition_zh: 量子物理学；研究量子现象及其规律的物理学分支
definition_en: the branch of physics that studies phenomena governed by discrete energy states and quantum rules
core_image: 一块烧红的铁在暗处发亮，颜色随温度改变，而解释这颜色的钥匙藏在一格一格的能级里
scene: 十九世纪末，物理学家困惑于炽热金属为何呈现某种颜色。Quantum physics grew out of attempts to explain the colour of hot metal.
sceneCN: 这里 quantum physics 指「研究量子现象的物理学分支」（第 1 个义项：以分立能量状态解释微观现象的学科）；句意：量子物理学源于解释炽热金属为何呈现某种颜色的努力。图中可辨识物件：烧红的金属块、光谱带、温度计、计算纸。

pos.zh: 量子物理学（不可数，作主语时视为单数）

senses.title: The branch that studies quantum effects
senses.titleCN: 研究量子效应的物理学分支
senses.definition: the area of physics concerned with systems whose behaviour is governed by discrete quantum states
senses.definitionCN: 研究行为受分立量子态支配的系统的物理学领域
senses.example: Quantum physics explains effects that classical physics cannot.
senses.exampleCN: 量子物理学解释了经典物理学无法解释的效应。
senses.why: Physics is the Greek-derived name for the study of nature, and quantum limits that study to the discrete scale.
senses.whyCN: 物理学是源自希腊语的「自然之学」，量子一词则把这门学问限定在分立尺度上。

senses.title: The phenomena themselves
senses.definition: the collection of observed effects, such as tunnelling or superposition, that the branch describes
senses.definitionCN: 该分支所描述的一整类观测效应，如隧穿或叠加
senses.example: Tunnelling is one of the clearest examples of quantum physics in action.
senses.exampleCN: 隧穿是量子物理在实际运作中最清楚的例子之一。
senses.why: A field's name often shifts from the study to its subject matter, so the phrase can mean the effects rather than the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 学科名常从「研究」滑向「研究对象」，因此这个短语也可以指效应本身而非学科。

senses.title: The university course
senses.definition: the taught subject in which the principles and calculations of the field are introduced
senses.definitionCN: 介绍该领域原理与计算的讲授科目
senses.example: The department offers quantum physics in the spring term.
senses.exampleCN: 该系在春季学期开设量子物理。
senses.why: Every established branch becomes a timetable entry, so the name also labels a course rather than a research programme.
senses.whyCN: 每个成熟分支都会变成课程表上的一栏，因此这个名字也指一门课，而非研究计划。

senses.title: The research community and its labs
senses.definition: the working community, its instruments and its projects, as in 'quantum physics needs bigger machines'
senses.definitionCN: 指从事该领域的人群、仪器与项目，如「量子物理需要更大的机器」
senses.example: Quantum physics now needs cryogenic labs as much as theory.
senses.exampleCN: 量子物理如今既需要理论，也同样需要低温实验室。
senses.why: Metonymy lets a discipline stand for the people and equipment that practise it, a common shift in academic speech.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让学科名代替实践它的人与设备，这是学术语言里常见的位移。

senses.title: The classical limit
senses.titleCN: 与经典物理的衔接极限
senses.definition: the way quantum rules reduce to ordinary classical behaviour for large or warm objects
senses.definitionCN: 对于巨大或温热的物体，量子规则退回普通经典行为的方式
senses.example: The border between quantum physics and everyday physics is a matter of scale.
senses.exampleCN: 量子物理与日常物理之间的界线是一个尺度问题。
senses.why: The branch must explain why the visible world is not visibly quantum, so its boundary with classical physics became a topic of its own.
senses.whyCN: 这一分支必须解释可见世界为何看不出量子性，因此它与经典物理的边界自成一个专题。

senses.title: The measurement problem
senses.definition: the unresolved questions about when a probability becomes a single observed outcome
senses.definitionCN: 关于概率何时变成单一观测结果的那些未决问题
senses.example: The measurement problem sits at the foundations of quantum physics.
senses.exampleCN: 测量问题位于量子物理的基础之处。
senses.why: Because the theory predicts odds rather than outcomes, the act of measuring raises questions the equations do not settle.
senses.whyCN: 理论预测的是几率而非结果，因此测量这一动作提出了方程无法解决的问题。

senses.title: The popular account of the field
senses.definition: books, articles and talks that present the field to non-specialists
senses.definitionCN: 向非专业读者介绍该领域的书、文章与讲座
senses.example: The shelf of popular quantum physics keeps growing.
senses.exampleCN: 大众量子物理的书架一直在变长。
senses.why: A subject that reshapes common sense attracts explainers, and the field's name becomes a publishing category.
senses.whyCN: 一门改写常识的学科会吸引解读者，学科名于是成了出版类别。

senses.title: The basis of quantum technologies
senses.definition: the physics behind devices such as quantum computers, sensors and secure communication
senses.definitionCN: 量子计算机、传感器与安全通信等装置背后的物理原理
senses.example: Quantum physics is now an engineering resource, not only a theory.
senses.exampleCN: 量子物理如今是一种工程资源，而不只是理论。
senses.why: Once quantum effects could be controlled, the science behind them was named in the same phrase as the industry built on it.
senses.whyCN: 量子效应可以被控制之后，其背后的科学便与建立其上的产业共用同一个说法。

intro.en: Quantum physics joins Latin quantum 'how much' to physics, from Greek physis 'nature' through Latin physica. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: quantum physics 把拉丁语「多少」接到 physics 上，而 physics 经拉丁 physica 出自希腊语「自然」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Physis meant 'nature, the natural order', from phyein 'to grow, to bring forth'. The verb's deeper origin is not settled.
items.cn: physis 意为「自然、自然秩序」，出自「生长、生出」的动词。该动词更早的来源没有定论。

items.en: Latin physica named the study of nature, borrowed from the Greek title of such works, and English physics came through that form.
items.cn: 拉丁 physica 指自然之学，借自这类希腊著作的书名，英语的 physics 即由此而来。

items.en: The neuter of quantus 'how much' entered physics in 1900 as the name of the smallest energy packet.
items.cn: 表示「多少」的中性形式在 1900 年作为最小能量包之名进入物理学。

items.en: As the new rules explained spectra, black-body radiation and atomic stability, the whole branch came to be called quantum physics.
items.cn: 当新规则解释了光谱、黑体辐射与原子稳定性之后，整个分支便被称为量子物理。

items.en: Quantum information and quantum technology gave the old branch a second life as an engineering field.
items.cn: 量子信息与量子技术让这个老分支作为工程领域获得第二次生命。

items.en: The first written uses of the exact English phrase are approximate; the Greek and Latin bases are well attested.
items.cn: 这个英语短语最早的书证年代为约数；希腊与拉丁来源都有充分记录。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the nature-root or sharing the physics name; group two holds neighbouring branches often mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「自然」词根或共享物理之名的词；第二组是常被当作同一回事的邻近分支。

entries.definition: The whole science of matter, energy and motion; quantum physics is one branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量与运动的整门科学；量子物理是其中一支。

entries.definition: Through French, the same nature-root came to mean the build of a person's body, not a science.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语，同一「自然」词根转指人的体格，而非一门科学。

entries.definition: Originally 'a natural philosopher', later a doctor of medicine; the root is shared with physics but the trade is different.
entries.definitionCN: 原指「自然哲学者」，后指医生；词根与物理学相同，行当却不同。

entries.definition: Relating to matter or the body, or to physics as a subject; it is the adjective that quantum physics does not use.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质的、身体的，或物理学的；它是形容词形式，而「量子物理」这一说法不用这一形式。

entries.definition: The precise theory of discrete states and probabilities; quantum physics is the broader branch that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 关于分立状态与概率的精确理论；量子物理是包含它的更大分支。

entries.definition: The physics of Newton and Maxwell, with continuous quantities; it is the limit quantum physics must recover at large scales.
entries.definitionCN: 牛顿与麦克斯韦的物理学，使用连续量；它是量子物理在大尺度上必须重现的极限。

entries.definition: The study of fundamental particles and their interactions; it relies on quantum physics but is not the same branch.
entries.definitionCN: 研究基本粒子及其相互作用；它依赖量子物理，但不是同一分支。

entries.definition: The union of quantum physics with fields and relativity; it is a further step, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 量子物理与场、相对论的结合；它是更进一步的理论，而非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: quantum 'how much' plus physics 'the study of nature': the study of nature in discrete amounts.
normal.cn: 「多少」加「自然之学」：按分立之量研究自然。

normal.en: The family runs quantum physics, quantum physicist, quantum theory, quantum mechanics.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括量子物理、量子物理学家、量子理论、量子力学。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: modern quantum physics, quantum physics laboratory, foundations of quantum physics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：现代量子物理、量子物理实验室、量子物理基础。

normal.en: Physics itself comes from the Greek word for nature, so the branch name literally means nature-study of quanta.
normal.cn: 物理学本身出自希腊语的「自然」，因此分支名字面上就是「量子的自然之学」。

normal.en: The field was born from the colour of hot metal, a problem classical physics could not solve.
normal.cn: 这个领域诞生于炽热金属的颜色，一个经典物理无法解决的问题。

abstract.en: Picture a glowing bar whose colour is a code for the steps hidden inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根发亮的金属条，它的颜色是内部台阶的密码。

abstract.en: Picture a rule book that governs the smallest things yet still explains the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一本只管最小之物的规则书，却仍能解释整个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a laboratory where the coldest machines study the smallest jumps.
abstract.cn: 想象一间实验室，最冷的机器研究最小的跳跃。

examples.en: Quantum physics began with the problem of black-body radiation.
examples.cn: 量子物理始于黑体辐射的问题。

examples.en: She teaches quantum physics to first-year engineers.
examples.cn: 她给一年级工科学生讲量子物理。

examples.en: Quantum physics underpins the new generation of sensors.
examples.cn: 量子物理支撑着新一代传感器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「quantum（量子）+ physics（物理）」——研究量子那一层的物理，就是量子物理

root: quantum（拉丁「多少」，量子）+ physics（拉丁 physica，出自希腊 physis「自然」）。英语 quantum physics。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the discipline to the phenomena, the course, the labs, the classical boundary, the measurement puzzle, popular books and finally the technology built on it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科走到现象、课程、实验室、经典边界、测量疑难、普及读物，最后是建立其上的技术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hot bar whose colour encodes the discrete steps hidden inside the metal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根炽热的金属条，颜色编码着金属内部隐藏的分立台阶。

branches.en: STUDY AND SUBJECT: the branch and the effects it studies are the same name seen from two ends.
branches.cn: 学问与对象：分支与它所研究的效应，是同一个名字的两端。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: a timetable entry and a community with cryogenic machines are two social faces of the field.
branches.cn: 人群：课程表上的一栏与一群使用低温机器的人，是这一领域的两个社会面孔。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the branch must show how its rules fade into ordinary physics.
branches.cn: 边界：这一分支必须说明它的规则如何淡入普通物理。

branches.en: THE PUZZLE: probability becoming one outcome remains unexplained at the foundations.
branches.cn: 疑难：概率如何变成一个结果，在基础处仍无解释。

branches.en: THE STORY AND THE MACHINE: the field becomes a shelf of popular books and a set of engineered devices.
branches.cn: 故事与机器：这一领域既变成一排普及读物，也变成一组工程装置。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin quantity word with the Greek-derived name of the whole science of nature.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的数量词与源自希腊的整门自然之学名称配对。

latinIntro.en: Latin quantum gives the first half; Latin physica, from Greek physis, gives the second and also yields physician, physical and physique.
latinIntro.cn: 前半由拉丁 quantum 提供；后半来自希腊 physis 经拉丁 physica，并衍生出 physician、physical、physique。

items.example: The first word fixes the scale of the study.
items.exampleCN: 第一个词固定了研究的尺度。

items.example: The root names everything that grows of itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指一切自行生长之物。

items.example: Medieval physica covered the whole natural world.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪的自然之学涵盖整个自然世界。

items.meaning: the science of matter and energy
items.meaningCN: 研究物质与能量的科学
items.example: Physics asks what heat actually is.
items.exampleCN: 物理学追问热究竟是什么。

items.example: Quantum physics explains the spectra of stars.
items.exampleCN: 量子物理解释恒星的光谱。

items.example: The quantum physicist adjusted the laser.
items.exampleCN: 这位量子物理学家调好了激光。

items.meaning: relating to matter or to physics
items.meaningCN: 与物质或物理学有关的
items.example: The physical world follows measurable rules.
items.exampleCN: 物质世界遵循可测量的规则。

items.example: The physician read the chart twice.
items.exampleCN: 医生把病历看了两遍。

physica, physicae (f., first declension, from Greek physis)

definition_zh: 振动；颤动；（手机等）震动；因情绪而发抖；在有节律地来回摆动
definition_en: to move quickly and continuously back and forth, or to shake with small rapid movements
core_image: 一根绷紧的弦被拨了一下，中间鼓起又凹下，空气跟着一收一放
scene: 歌手唱到高处，薄金属片开始来回抖动。The thin metal plate began to vibrate when the singer held a high note.
sceneCN: 这里 vibrate 指「快速来回摆动」（第 1 个义项：物体围绕平衡位置作快速往复运动）；句意：歌手唱出一个高音时，薄金属片开始振动。图中可辨识物件：金属片、声波弧线、歌者、支架。

derivatives.zh: 颤音（演奏或演唱的装饰）
有活力的；鲜艳的（由「振动」引申）

senses.title: Move rapidly back and forth
senses.definition: to move repeatedly to and fro about a fixed position, as a string or a membrane does
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个固定位置反复来回运动，如弦或膜那样
senses.example: The string vibrates at four hundred cycles per second.
senses.exampleCN: 这根弦每秒振动四百个周期。
senses.why: Latin vibrare meant 'to shake, to move rapidly', and the physical sense keeps exactly that gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义是「摇动、快速移动」，物理义保留的正是这个动作。

senses.title: Produce sound through such movement
senses.definition: to make a sound by rapid movement, as vocal cords or a loudspeaker do
senses.definitionCN: 靠快速运动发出声音，如声带或扬声器那样
senses.example: Her vocal cords vibrate as the breath passes through them.
senses.exampleCN: 气息通过时，她的声带发生振动。
senses.why: Sound is air pushed in pulses, and a vibrating surface supplies those pulses, so the verb also means to give voice.
senses.whyCN: 声音是被推成一串脉冲的空气，振动的表面提供这些脉冲，因此这个动词也指发声。

senses.title: A phone or device buzzes
senses.definition: to shake with a rapid hum as a silent signal, as a phone set to silent mode does
senses.definitionCN: 以快速的嗡嗡抖动作为无声提示，如静音模式的手机
senses.example: The phone vibrated twice in his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 手机在他口袋里震了两下。
senses.why: A tiny motor spins an off-centre weight, and the whole casing repeats the old shaking gesture on a small scale.
senses.whyCN: 微型马达带着偏心块旋转，整个外壳便在小尺度上重复了那个古老的摇动动作。

senses.title: Quiver with strong feeling
senses.definition: to tremble visibly under anger, fear or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 因愤怒、恐惧或激动而明显发抖
senses.example: He vibrated with rage but said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他气得发抖，却一言不发。
senses.why: The body really does shake under strong feeling, so the physical verb became the natural word for visible emotion.
senses.whyCN: 强烈情绪下身体确实会抖，因此这个物理动词自然成了可见情绪的用词。

senses.title: Atoms and bonds vibrate
senses.definition: to oscillate at the molecular level, as bonded atoms do when heated
senses.definitionCN: 在分子层面来回摆动，如受热时成键原子那样
senses.example: The bonds vibrate faster as the sample warms.
senses.exampleCN: 样品升温时，化学键振动得更快。
senses.why: Heat is molecular motion, and the motion of bonded atoms is a spring-like oscillation, so the everyday verb fits the smallest scale.
senses.whyCN: 热就是分子运动，而成键原子的运动像弹簧一样往复，因此日常动词也适用于最小尺度。

senses.title: Respond to another vibration
senses.definition: to shake because a nearby object is already shaking at a matching rate
senses.definitionCN: 因附近物体以相合的速率振动而跟着抖动
senses.example: The window vibrated in time with the bass.
senses.exampleCN: 窗户随着低音一起振动。
senses.why: When two objects share a natural rate, one can drive the other, and the verb describes this sympathetic response.
senses.whyCN: 当两个物体共享同一自然速率时，一个能驱动另一个，这个动词描述的正是这种应和。

senses.title: Shake under strain or traffic
senses.definition: to shake because of mechanical stress, as a bridge or a building does under load
senses.definitionCN: 因机械应力而抖动，如承重时的桥或建筑
senses.example: The bridge vibrated as the column marched across.
senses.exampleCN: 队列走过时，桥身发生振动。
senses.why: Engineering borrowed the word for unwanted shaking because the movement is the same, only the cause is different.
senses.whyCN: 工程界借这个词指不受欢迎的抖动，因为动作相同，只是成因不同。

senses.title: Swing between two readings
senses.titleCN: 在两个读数之间来回摆动
senses.definition: to move repeatedly between two states or values without settling
senses.definitionCN: 在两个状态或数值之间反复移动而不稳定下来
senses.example: The needle vibrated between two readings for a full minute.
senses.exampleCN: 指针在两个读数之间来回摆动了整整一分钟。
senses.why: The back-and-forth shape of physical vibration became a figure for anything that will not settle on one value.
senses.whyCN: 物理振动来回往复的形状，成了任何无法稳定在一个数值之物的一般比喻。

intro.en: Vibrate comes from Latin vibrare 'to shake, to move rapidly to and fro'. The deeper origin of that verb is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vibrate 来自拉丁 vibrare「摇动、快速来回移动」。这个动词更早的来源尚无定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vibrare meant 'to shake, to brandish, to move with a quivering motion'. It described both a hand waving a weapon and a string in motion.
items.cn: vibrare 意为「摇动、挥舞、以抖动的方式移动」，既可描述挥动武器的手，也可描述运动的弦。

items.en: The derived noun vibratio named a shaking or a quivering, and this is the shape English later borrowed for the scientific term.
items.cn: 派生名词 vibratio 指摇动或颤动，英语后来借用的正是这一形态，用于科学术语。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century, first for things that shake physically and soon for sounds and feelings.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，最初指物体实体地抖动，很快扩展到声音与情绪。

items.en: With the study of sound and elasticity the word became technical, naming regular oscillation about a fixed point.
items.cn: 随着声学与弹性研究的发展，这个词变成技术用语，指围绕固定点的规则往复运动。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the Latin verb is well attested, but no earlier form is agreed, and suggested links to other Indo-European shaking words remain reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：这个拉丁动词本身有充分书证，但更早的形式没有定论，把它与其他印欧语「摇动」词联系起来的说法仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same shaking root; group two holds near verbs that describe slightly different kinds of trembling.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「摇动」词根的词；第二组是描述不同类型的抖动的近义动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the movement itself, or for a single cycle of it; it is the direct derivative, not a separate idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指这一运动本身或其中一个周期的名词；它是直接派生词，并非另一个概念。

entries.definition: Originally 'vibrating', now mostly 'full of life or bright', a figurative shift from rapid movement to liveliness.
entries.definitionCN: 原义为「振动的」，如今多指「有活力的、鲜艳的」，是从快速运动到生气的比喻转移。

entries.definition: An Italian musical term for a deliberate wavering of pitch, built on the same Latin shaking verb.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语音乐术语，指有意让音高微微起伏，构于同一个拉丁「摇动」动词。

entries.definition: A device that shakes, from the same root plus an agent suffix; it names the machine, not the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 会抖动的装置，由同一词根加施动后缀构成；它指机器，而非运动。

entries.definition: The general word for short irregular movements; vibrate usually implies a faster, more regular back-and-forth.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指短促而不规则的移动；这个词通常暗示更快、更规则的往复。

entries.definition: The technical verb for swinging regularly between two points, often used of pendulums and currents.
entries.definitionCN: 技术用语，指在两点之间规则摆动，常用于摆与电流。

entries.definition: To shake with very small rapid movements, often from weakness or emotion rather than mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 以极小而快的动作抖动，常因虚弱或情绪而非机械原因。

entries.definition: To shake involuntarily, typically of a person from cold, fear or weakness.
entries.definitionCN: 不自主地抖动，通常指人因寒冷、恐惧或虚弱而抖。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin vibrare 'to shake': the word is the shake itself.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「摇动」：这个词就是抖动本身。

normal.en: The family runs vibrate, vibration, vibrational, vibrator, vibrato, vibrant.
normal.cn: 同族词包括振动、振动（名词）、振动的、振动器、颤音、有活力的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: vibrate with anger, vibrate at a frequency, set the air vibrating.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：气得发抖、以某一频率振动、使空气振动。

normal.en: A phone on silent mode vibrates, which is the old shake shrunk to a pocket.
normal.cn: 静音手机震动，就是那古老的摇动缩进了口袋。

normal.en: Vibrant and vibrato both come from this root, one by metaphor and one by music.
normal.cn: 「有活力的」与「颤音」都出自这个词根，一个靠比喻，一个靠音乐。

abstract.en: Picture a plucked string that keeps its shape in the air long after the finger leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象被拨动的弦，手指离开后仍在空气里留着形状。

abstract.en: Picture a struck bell whose whole body is the sound.
abstract.cn: 想象被敲响的钟，整个身体就是声音。

abstract.en: Picture a needle that cannot choose between two numbers and keeps crossing the gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指针在两个数字之间无法选择，只好不断越过空隙。

examples.en: The membrane vibrates when sound reaches it.
examples.cn: 声音到达时，膜片发生振动。

examples.en: The whole floor vibrated as the lorry passed.
examples.cn: 卡车经过时，整层地板都在震动。

examples.en: His voice vibrated with barely controlled anger.
examples.cn: 他的声音因几乎压不住的怒气而发抖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vibr（摇）+ ate（动词尾）」——不停地摇，就是振动

root: 拉丁 vibrare「摇动、快速来回移动」，更早来源不确定；派生名词 vibratio。英语 vibrate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep one back-and-forth gesture: a string, a voice, a phone, a body in rage, a chemical bond, a sympathetic window, a strained bridge and finally a needle that will not settle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个来回动作：一根弦、一副嗓音、一部手机、一具愤怒的身体、一根化学键、一扇应和的窗、一座受压的桥，最后是一根不肯稳定的指针。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretched string bulging and dipping while the air around it pulses in step.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绷紧的弦鼓起又凹下，周围的空气随之同步起伏。

branches.en: ONE MOVEMENT AT TWO SCALES: a string and a chemical bond perform the same spring-like back-and-forth.
branches.cn: 同一动作的两个尺度：弦与化学键做着同样像弹簧一样的往复。

branches.en: SOUND: the shaking surface pushes the air into pulses, so the movement becomes audible.
branches.cn: 声音：振动的表面把空气推成一串脉冲，运动于是变得可听。

branches.en: TRANSMITTED SHAKING: a motor, a bass note and marching feet all pass the same tremor to another object.
branches.cn: 传递的抖动：马达、低音与行进的脚步，都把同一种颤动传给另一物体。

branches.en: THE BODY: strong feeling produces a real tremor, so emotion is described with the physical verb.
branches.cn: 身体：强烈情绪会产生真实的颤动，因此情绪也用这个物理动词来描述。

branches.en: THE UNRESOLVED VALUE: the back-and-forth becomes a figure for indecision between two readings.
branches.cn: 未定的数值：来回运动成了在两个读数之间摇摆不定的比喻。

intro.en: Vibrate is a Latin verb whose stem also builds a large English family of nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: vibrate 是一个拉丁动词，其词干还在英语里造出一大批名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vibrare gives vibrate, vibration and vibrato through Italian; the same stem is behind vibrant, where the shaking has turned into liveliness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vibrare 衍生 vibrate、vibration，并经意大利语衍生 vibrato；同一词干还在 vibrant 背后，那里的「抖动」已转为「有生气」。

items.example: The verb describes rapid motion in place.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述在原地的快速运动。

items.example: The ending carries the borrowed Latin verb into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把借来的拉丁动词带进英语。

items.example: The plate vibrates at a fixed rate.
items.exampleCN: 薄片以固定速率振动。

items.meaning: the act or instance of shaking
items.meaningCN: 抖动的动作或一次抖动
items.example: The vibration lasted several seconds.
items.exampleCN: 这次振动持续了好几秒。

items.example: Vibrational energy is stored in the bonds.
items.exampleCN: 振动能量储存在化学键里。

items.example: The vibrator alerted him without sound.
items.exampleCN: 振动器在没有声音的情况下提醒了他。

items.example: The singer added vibrato to the long note.
items.exampleCN: 歌手在长音上加了颤音。

items.example: The market was vibrant at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 清晨的市场充满生气。

latinEntries.structure: vibrare, vibro, vibravi, vibratum (v., first conjugation)

definition_zh: 共振；共鸣；洪亮的回响；物理学中系统在特定频率下的强响应
definition_en: a strong sympathetic vibration produced when a system is driven at its natural frequency, or the deep echoing quality of a sound
core_image: 一个长音正好撞上玻璃杯的固有节律，杯壁越摆越大，直到裂开
scene: 歌剧演员唱出一个长音，玻璃杯突然裂开。The glass shattered because the note matched its resonance exactly.
sceneCN: 这里 resonance 指「系统在固有频率下产生的强响应」（第 1 个义项：外驱频率与固有频率相合时的剧烈振动）；句意：玻璃杯碎裂，是因为那个音正好与它的共振频率相合。图中可辨识物件：玻璃杯、歌者、声波环、碎裂纹。

pos.zh: 共振；共鸣；回响（可数或不可数）

senses.title: Driven vibration at a natural frequency
senses.titleCN: 在固有频率下被驱动的强振动
senses.definition: the large vibration that occurs when a system is pushed at the rate it naturally prefers
senses.definitionCN: 当系统被以它天然偏好的速率推动时出现的剧烈振动
senses.example: The bridge collapsed when wind matched its resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 风与桥的共振相合时，桥塌了。
senses.why: Latin resonare means 'to sound again', and a system driven at its own rate answers every push with a larger one, so the name records the answering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语意为「再次发声」，而被以自身速率驱动的系统会对每一次推动给出更大的回应，名字记下的正是这种回应。

senses.title: A deep, full sound
senses.definition: the rich, prolonged quality of a sound that seems to fill a space
senses.definitionCN: 一种似乎填满空间的丰厚而持久的声音品质
senses.example: The cello's low strings have a warm resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴的低音弦有温暖的共鸣。
senses.why: A body that answers many frequencies at once sounds full, so the physical response became a word for tonal richness.
senses.whyCN: 能同时应和许多频率的物体听起来饱满，因此物理响应成了音色丰厚的说法。

senses.title: Magnetic resonance imaging
senses.definition: the technique in which atomic nuclei in a magnetic field absorb and re-emit radio waves at characteristic frequencies
senses.definitionCN: 原子核在磁场中于特征频率吸收并再发射无线电波的技术
senses.example: The scan uses magnetic resonance to map soft tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 这项扫描利用磁共振来成像软组织。
senses.why: Nuclei are tiny magnets with fixed precession rates, and flipping them at exactly that rate is resonance in the strict physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 原子核是带固定进动速率的小磁体，恰好在那个速率上把它翻转，就是严格物理意义上的共振。

senses.title: Resonance in chemical bonding
senses.definition: the description of a molecule as a weighted blend of several possible electron arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 把分子描述为几种可能电子排布的加权混合
senses.example: Benzene is drawn as resonance between two ring structures.
senses.exampleCN: 苯被画成两种环状结构之间的共振。
senses.why: Chemists borrowed the word because the true electron pattern behaves like a system answering several forms at once.
senses.whyCN: 化学家借这个词，是因为真实的电子分布像同时应和几种形式的系统。

senses.title: Emotional or cultural echo
senses.definition: the quality of an idea, story or image that stirs a strong shared response in an audience
senses.definitionCN: 一个想法、故事或形象在受众中激起强烈共同回应的品质
senses.example: The film found resonance with readers who had also left home.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在同样离家的读者中引起了共鸣。
senses.why: Sympathetic vibration is a ready metaphor for a feeling that is set off in one person by something in another.
senses.whyCN: 应和振动天然适合比喻一种由他人之物在自身激起的感受。

senses.title: Regular gravitational timing
senses.definition: a situation in which orbiting bodies repeatedly pull on one another in a fixed rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 轨道上的天体以固定节律反复相互牵引的情形
senses.example: The moons are locked in orbital resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 这些卫星被锁在轨道共振之中。
senses.why: The repeated gravitational pushes arrive at the same phase of each orbit, which is the astronomical version of driving a system at its own rate.
senses.whyCN: 反复的引力推动落在每次轨道的同一相位上，这正是「以自身速率驱动系统」的天文版本。

senses.title: A short-lived particle state
senses.definition: a very brief particle state that appears as a peak in a scattering experiment
senses.definitionCN: 在散射实验里表现为峰值的极短暂粒子状态
senses.example: The team reported a new resonance in the collision data.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在碰撞数据中报告了一个新的共振态。
senses.why: A particle that lives too briefly to be seen leaves a peak at one energy, the same signature as a driven oscillator.
senses.whyCN: 寿命短到看不见的粒子会在某一能量处留下峰值，其印记与受驱振子相同。

senses.title: Tuned response in a circuit
senses.definition: the condition in which an electrical circuit responds most strongly at one chosen frequency
senses.definitionCN: 电路在某一选定频率上响应最强的状态
senses.example: The radio circuit reaches resonance at the station's frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机电路在电台频率上达到共振。
senses.why: Capacitance and inductance exchange energy in a rhythm, and matching an incoming signal to that rhythm is electrical resonance.
senses.whyCN: 电容与电感按节律交换能量，把来信号与这一节律相合，就是电学共振。

intro.en: Resonance comes from Latin resonantia 'echo', from resonare 'to sound again', built on re- 'again' and sonare 'to sound'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: resonance 来自拉丁 resonantia「回声」，而它出自 resonare「再次发声」，由「再次」与「发声」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sonus meant 'sound, tone'. Its deeper origin is not established; the usual link to a root meaning 'to sound' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: sonus 意为「声音、音调」。其更早来源没有定论；把它与表示「发声」的词根联系起来的说法属于重构。

items.en: Resonare meant 'to resound, to return a sound', as a hall or a cave returns a shout.
items.cn: resonare 意为「回响、把声音送回来」，如厅堂或洞穴把喊声送回。

items.en: The noun resonantia named an echo or a re-echoing, the abstract result of that returning sound.
items.cn: 名词 resonantia 指回声或反复回响，是那种返回之声的抽象结果。

items.en: English borrowed resonance in the sixteenth century for an echoing sound, and it remained chiefly a word about acoustics.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 resonance，指回响的声音，长期主要是声学词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century physics applied it to any system driven at its natural rate, and chemistry, astronomy and medicine each took a share.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，物理学把它用于任何被自身速率驱动的系统，化学、天文学与医学各取一支。

items.en: First dates for the technical senses are approximate; the Latin chain is fully recorded.
items.cn: 各技术义的最早年代为约数；拉丁语链条有完整记录。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words and one dangerous look-alike from a different root; group two holds near sound and vibration words.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词与一个来自不同词根的易混形近词；第二组是邻近的声音与振动词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing something that resounds or is driven at its natural rate; it is not a separate physical effect.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物回响或在其固有速率上被驱动的形容词；它不是另一种物理效应。

entries.definition: From Latin residere 'to remain sitting', built on sedere 'to sit': a place where one lives, with no sound involved.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「留在坐着」，构于「坐」：指居住之所，与声音无关。

entries.definition: Latin con- 'together' plus sonare: sounds that agree when played together, a musical judgement rather than a driven vibration.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁「共同」加「发声」：合奏时相合的声音，是音乐判断而非受驱振动。

entries.definition: Latin dis- 'apart' plus sonare: sounds that clash, the opposite judgement to consonance and unrelated to resonance.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁「分开」加「发声」：相冲的声音，与「协和」相反，也与共振无关。

entries.definition: A sound reflected back once from a surface; resonance is a sustained response, not a single bounce.
entries.definitionCN: 声音从一个表面反射回来一次；而这个词指持续响应，不是一次反弹。

entries.definition: The prolonging of sound by repeated reflections in a room; it is the acoustic result that resonance can help produce.
entries.definitionCN: 声音在室内经多次反射而延长；它是共振可能促成的声学结果。

entries.definition: Any rapid back-and-forth movement; resonance is the special case where the movement grows because it is driven at the right rate.
entries.definitionCN: 任何快速的往复运动；这个词是其特例，因被以正确速率驱动而增大。

entries.definition: A feeling shared with another person; the word was once used for physical sympathetic vibration and now mostly means emotional agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人共享的感受；这个词曾用于物理上的应和振动，如今多指情感上的相合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin re- 'again' plus sonare 'to sound': a sound that answers again and again.
normal.cn: 拉丁「再次」加「发声」：一再应答的声音。

normal.en: The family runs resonance, resonant, resonate, resonator, resonantly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括共振、洪亮的、共鸣、共鸣器、以共鸣的方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: magnetic resonance, resonance frequency, emotional resonance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：磁共振、共振频率、情感共鸣。

normal.en: The same sound-root appears in consonant and dissonant, both judgements of harmony.
normal.cn: 同一「发声」词根出现在协和与不协和里，两者都是对和声的判断。

normal.en: Beware residence: it comes from sitting, not sounding, and only looks alike.
normal.cn: 当心那个表示「居住」的形近词：它出自「坐」而非「发声」，只是长得像。

abstract.en: Picture a swing pushed at exactly the moment it comes back, so each push adds height.
abstract.cn: 想象秋千荡回的那一刻恰好被推一下，于是每一推都增加高度。

abstract.en: Picture a room that repeats a single note until the note seems to own the space.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间反复送回同一个音，直到那个音仿佛占有了空间。

abstract.en: Picture two tuning forks of the same pitch, one waking the other without being touched.
abstract.cn: 想象两支同音高的音叉，一支未被触碰却唤醒了另一支。

examples.en: The singer broke the glass by finding its resonance.
examples.cn: 歌手找到玻璃的共振点，把它唱碎了。

examples.en: The poem has a resonance that outlasts its century.
examples.cn: 这首诗有一种超越它那个时代的共鸣。

examples.en: The circuit is tuned to resonance at one frequency only.
examples.cn: 这个电路只在一个频率上被调到共振。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ son（声）+ ance」——声音一再回来，就是共鸣

root: 拉丁 resonantia「回声」← resonare「再次发声」= re-「再次」+ sonare「发声」；sonus「声音」更早来源不确定。英语 resonance。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one pattern of answering: a driven system, a full tone, a medical scan, a chemical blend, an emotional echo, an orbital rhythm, a particle peak and a tuned circuit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个「应答」模式：受驱系统、饱满音色、医学扫描、化学混合、情感回声、轨道节律、粒子峰值与调谐电路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note that matches a glass's own rhythm, so every push arrives at the right moment and the swing grows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个与玻璃固有节律相合的音，每次推动都恰好落在对的时刻，摆幅便越来越大。

branches.en: THE DRIVEN SYSTEM: a glass and a radio circuit both grow loud when pushed at their own rate.
branches.cn: 受驱系统：玻璃杯与收音机电路在被以自身速率推动时都会变得强烈。

branches.en: THE FULL VOICE: a body answering many rates at once sounds rich and prolonged.
branches.cn: 饱满的声音：同时应和许多速率的物体听起来丰厚而持久。

branches.en: THE MEASURED PEAK: nuclei and short-lived particles both mark resonance as a sharp maximum in a scan.
branches.cn: 被测的峰：原子核与短命粒子都把共振表现为扫描图上的尖峰。

branches.en: THE BLEND: chemistry uses the word for a molecule that answers several electron arrangements at once.
branches.cn: 混合：化学用这个词指同时应和几种电子排布的分子。

branches.en: THE RHYTHM ELSEWHERE: a story stirs a shared feeling, and moons pull one another in step.
branches.cn: 别处的节律：故事激起共同感受，卫星则同步相互牵引。

intro.en: Resonance is a Latin abstract noun built from a prefix, a verb of sounding and a noun ending, all three of which recur in English.
intro.cn: resonance 是拉丁抽象名词，由前缀、发声动词与名词结尾构成，三者在英语里都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sonare and sonus also give consonant, dissonant, sonata and sonar's namesake; re- adds the idea of return.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sonare 与 sonus 还衍生出 consonant、dissonant、sonata 以及 sonar 的同源成分；re- 增添「返回」之意。

items.example: The prefix marks a movement that comes back.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出折返的运动。

items.example: The verb covers any sounding, sung or struck.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词涵盖任何发声，唱或敲皆可。

items.example: The noun names the thing that returns.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被送回来的那个东西。

items.example: The hall resounded with the choir.
items.exampleCN: 大厅里回荡着合唱声。

items.example: The noun names the state of answering sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指声音应答的状态。

items.example: The note found the glass's resonance.
items.exampleCN: 那个音找到了玻璃的共振点。

items.example: A resonant voice fills the hall.
items.exampleCN: 洪亮的嗓音充满大厅。

items.meaning: to echo; to strike a shared feeling
items.example: The story resonated with the audience.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事在听众中引起共鸣。

latinEntries.structure: sonare, sono, sonavi, sonatum (v., first conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to sound, to make a noise

definition_zh: 洪亮的；回响的；引起共鸣的；共振的
definition_en: producing a deep prolonged sound, or responding strongly at a particular frequency; also stirring a shared feeling
core_image: 空厅里一个低音久久不散，墙与地板都跟着轻轻回应
scene: 合唱团离场很久，空荡的大厅里仍留着一阵低沉的回响。A resonant hum stayed in the empty hall long after the choir left.
sceneCN: 这里 resonant 指「深沉而持久的回响」（第 1 个义项：声音饱满并在空间中延续）；句意：合唱团离开很久之后，一阵洪亮的低鸣仍留在空荡的大厅里。图中可辨识物件：空座椅、穹顶、声波弧、木地板。

pos.zh: 洪亮的；回响的；共振的；引起共鸣的

senses.title: Deep and long-lasting in sound
senses.definition: of a sound: full, low and slow to fade, as if the space keeps returning it
senses.definitionCN: 指声音：饱满、低沉、消退缓慢，仿佛空间在不断把它送回来
senses.example: The resonant bass filled the wooden hall.
senses.exampleCN: 洪亮的低音充满了木制大厅。
senses.why: The Latin word is the present participle of 'to resound', so the adjective describes something that keeps sounding back.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词是「回响」的现在分词，因此形容词描述的是不断把声音送回来的东西。

senses.title: A space that returns sound
senses.titleCN: 会把声音送回来的空间
senses.definition: describing a room, cave or hall whose surfaces reflect sound strongly
senses.definitionCN: 描述墙面强烈反射声音的房间、洞穴或厅堂
senses.example: The resonant cave repeated every footstep twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这座回响的洞穴把每个脚步重复两遍。
senses.why: Hard curved surfaces send sound back instead of absorbing it, and the same adjective covers the place as covers the sound.
senses.whyCN: 坚硬弯曲的表面把声音送回而不吸收，因此同一个形容词既修饰声音也修饰地点。

senses.title: Stirring a shared feeling
senses.definition: of a word, image or event: producing a strong emotional response that many people recognise
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、形象或事件：激起许多人共有的强烈情感回应
senses.example: Her short farewell was more resonant than a long speech.
senses.exampleCN: 她简短的告别比一篇长演讲更能引起共鸣。
senses.why: Emotional response was modelled on physical resonance: one thing sets another vibrating in sympathy.
senses.whyCN: 情感回应是照着物理共振来理解的：一物使另一物应和振动。

senses.title: Responding at a natural frequency
senses.titleCN: 在固有频率上强烈响应
senses.definition: in physics: responding with a large amplitude when driven at the frequency the system prefers
senses.definitionCN: 物理学上：被以系统偏好的频率驱动时以大振幅响应
senses.example: The resonant mode of the crystal amplifies the signal.
senses.exampleCN: 晶体的共振模态放大了这个信号。
senses.why: A system pushed at its own rate stores energy instead of resisting it, so it answers far more strongly than at other rates.
senses.whyCN: 被以自身速率推动的系统会储存能量而非抵抗，因此响应远强于其他速率。

senses.title: A device built to resonate
senses.definition: describing a cavity, circuit or tube designed to hold and amplify one frequency
senses.definitionCN: 描述为容纳并放大某一频率而设计的腔体、电路或管
senses.example: The resonant cavity stores microwaves for a fraction of a second.
senses.exampleCN: 共振腔把微波储存几分之一秒。
senses.why: Once physics understood the effect, engineers built objects whose whole purpose is to be resonant.
senses.whyCN: 物理学理解这一效应之后，工程师就造出以「共振」为全部目的的物件。

senses.title: In tune with an idea or group
senses.titleCN: 与某种观念或群体相呼应
senses.definition: followed by with: closely connected to something and likely to stir agreement
senses.definitionCN: 后接表示「与」的介词：与某物紧密相连，容易激起认同
senses.example: The speech was resonant with the worries of the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲话与人群的忧虑相互呼应。
senses.why: The construction 'resonant with' keeps the physical idea of two things sharing a rate, transferred to shared concerns.
senses.whyCN: 「与……相呼应」这一结构保留了「两物共享同一速率」的物理想法，只是转到了共同关切上。

senses.title: A voice with body and depth
senses.definition: describing a voice that seems to come from a large, well-filled space
senses.definitionCN: 描述仿佛出自一个宽阔饱满空间的嗓音
senses.example: The actor's resonant voice carried to the back row.
senses.exampleCN: 演员洪亮的嗓音传到了最后一排。
senses.why: A chest voice excites more of the body's cavities, so acoustics supplies the everyday praise of a good speaking voice.
senses.whyCN: 胸腔发声会激起身体更多空腔，因此声学为日常对好嗓音的称赞提供了说法。

senses.title: An image that will not fade
senses.definition: of a name, image or phrase: continuing to be remembered and repeated long after it appears
senses.definitionCN: 指名称、形象或短语：出现很久之后仍被记住与引用
senses.example: The name remains resonant a century after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 那场罢工过去一个世纪，这个名字仍能引起回响。
senses.why: What stays in memory behaves like a sound that keeps returning, so the acoustic adjective became a word about lasting meaning.
senses.whyCN: 留在记忆里的东西，行为像不断返回的声音，于是这个声学形容词成了「意义持久」的说法。

intro.en: Resonant is the English form of Latin resonans, the present participle of resonare 'to sound again'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: resonant 是拉丁 resonans 的英语形式，而 resonans 是 resonare「再次发声」的现在分词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sonare meant 'to sound, to make a noise', and its noun sonus meant 'sound'. The deeper origin of the root is not established.
items.cn: sonare 意为「发声、发出响声」，其名词 sonus 意为「声音」。这个词根更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Re- 'again, back' plus sonare produced resonare, 'to resound, to send a sound back'.
items.cn: 「再次、返回」加「发声」构成 resonare，意为「回响、把声音送回来」。

items.en: The present participle resonans described anything currently resounding, and English took that form rather than the abstract noun.
items.cn: 现在分词 resonans 描述正在回响之物，英语采用的就是这一形式，而非抽象名词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the adjective covered both echoing spaces and full sounds, and later spread to figurative meaning.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个形容词既修饰回响的空间，也修饰饱满的声音，后来扩展到比喻意义。

items.en: Physics added the strict sense of a system driven at its natural frequency, and engineering added resonant cavities and circuits.
items.cn: 物理学增添了「系统被固有频率驱动」的严格义，工程学又增添了共振腔与共振电路。

items.en: The first dates for the technical senses are approximate; the Latin participle is fully attested.
items.cn: 各技术义的最早年代为约数；拉丁分词本身有完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same resounding root plus one look-alike from a sitting root; group two holds adjectives of sound and feeling.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「回响」词根的几种形式，外加一个出自「坐」词根的形近词；第二组是声音与感受方面的近义形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the effect itself, either the physical response or the emotional echo; the adjective describes what has it.
entries.definitionCN: 指效应本身的名词，既可指物理响应，也可指情感回声；形容词则描述具有这一效应之物。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to resound or to stir a shared feeling; it names the action that the adjective qualifies.
entries.definitionCN: 意为回响或激起共同感受的动词；它指形容词所修饰的那个动作。

entries.definition: From Latin residere 'to remain sitting', built on sedere 'to sit': a person who lives somewhere, with nothing acoustic about it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「留在坐着」，构于「坐」：指住在某处的人，与声音毫无关系。

entries.definition: An object or cavity designed to resonate, from the same root plus an agent suffix; it is the instrument, not the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 为共振而设计的物体或腔体，由同一词根加施动后缀构成；它指器具，而非性质。

entries.definition: From Latin sonorus 'full of sound': deep and rich in tone, but without the idea of being driven at a natural frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「充满声音」：音色深沉丰厚，但不含被固有频率驱动的意思。

entries.definition: Simply returning a sound from a surface; it lacks the sustained reinforcement that resonant implies.
entries.definitionCN: 只表示声音从表面返回来；缺少这个词所含的持续增强。

entries.definition: Bringing images or feelings to mind; it overlaps with the figurative sense of resonant but not with the acoustic one.
entries.definitionCN: 使形象或感受浮现；它与这个词的比喻义重叠，但不涉及声学义。

entries.definition: Originally 'vibrating', now 'full of life or bright'; it suggests energy rather than a returning sound.
entries.definitionCN: 原义「振动的」，今多指「有活力的、鲜艳的」；它暗示能量，而非返回的声音。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin re- 'again' plus sonare 'to sound': sounding again.
normal.cn: 拉丁「再次」加「发声」：再次发声。

normal.en: The family runs resonant, resonance, resonate, resonator, resonantly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括洪亮的、共振、共鸣、共鸣器、以回响的方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: resonant voice, resonant frequency, resonant cavity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：洪亮的嗓音、共振频率、共振腔。

normal.en: The phrase resonant with links the physical idea to shared feelings.
normal.cn: 「与……相呼应」这一搭配把物理概念接到共同感受上。

normal.en: Beware resident: it comes from sitting, not sounding.
normal.cn: 当心那个表示「居民」的形近词：它出自「坐」而非「发声」。

abstract.en: Picture a hall that keeps answering after the singer has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象歌者离开后仍在应答的厅堂。

abstract.en: Picture a word that keeps ringing in the mind years later.
abstract.cn: 想象一个多年后仍在脑中作响的词。

abstract.en: Picture a glass that grows louder the more exactly it is matched.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃杯被匹配得越准，响声就越大。

examples.en: His resonant voice needed no microphone.
examples.cn: 他洪亮的嗓音不需要扩音器。

examples.en: The chamber is resonant at one microwave frequency.
examples.cn: 这个腔体在一个微波频率上发生共振。

examples.en: The date is resonant for everyone in the room.
examples.cn: 这个日期让屋里每个人都心有回响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「reson（回响）+ ant（形容词尾）」——会一直回响的，就是洪亮共鸣的

root: 拉丁 resonans（resonare「再次发声」的现在分词）= re-「再次」+ sonare「发声」。英语 resonant。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe answering: a full sound, an echoing room, a stirred feeling, a driven system, a built cavity, an agreeing idea, a deep voice and an image that keeps returning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「应答」：饱满的声音、回响的房间、被激起的感受、受驱的系统、造出的腔体、相合的观念、深沉的嗓音，以及不断返回的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low note still hanging in an empty hall, answered faintly by walls and floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个低音仍悬在空厅里，墙壁与地板轻轻应和。

branches.en: THE VOICE: a full tone and a deep speaking voice are the same bodily resonance heard in two settings.
branches.cn: 嗓音：饱满的音与深沉的说话声，是同一身体共振在两种场合被听到。

branches.en: THE ROOM: hard surfaces return sound, so the place itself can be called resonant.
branches.cn: 房间：坚硬表面把声音送回，因此地点本身也能被称为回响的。

branches.en: THE SHARED FEELING: a word or speech answers a group's concerns, the emotional form of matching a frequency.
branches.cn: 共同感受：词语或讲话应和群体的关切，这是「频率相合」的情感形式。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERED RESPONSE: physics names the effect, and engineering builds cavities that exploit it.
branches.cn: 工程响应：物理学为效应命名，工程学则造出利用它的腔体。

branches.en: THE AFTERLIFE: what keeps being remembered behaves like a sound that will not stop returning.
branches.cn: 余响：被不断记住之物，行为像不肯停止返回的声音。

intro.en: Resonant is a Latin participle turned English adjective, with a prefix, a sounding verb and a participle ending.
intro.cn: resonant 是由拉丁分词转成的英语形容词，含一个前缀、一个发声动词与一个分词结尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin resonare and sonare also yield resonance, resonate, sonorous and consonance in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 resonare 与 sonare 在英语里还衍生出 resonance、resonate、sonorous 与 consonance。

items.example: The prefix marks a return of the sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出声音的返回。

items.example: The verb is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of ongoing action.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾造出表示持续动作的形容词。

items.example: The valley resounded after the bell.
items.exampleCN: 钟声之后山谷回响。

items.example: The resounding choir filled the nave.
items.exampleCN: 回响的合唱充满中殿。

items.example: A resonant note hung in the air.
items.exampleCN: 一个洪亮的音悬在空气里。

items.example: The cavity has a sharp resonance.
items.exampleCN: 这个腔体有一个尖锐的共振点。

items.meaning: to echo or stir a feeling
items.example: The image resonated with voters.
items.exampleCN: 这个形象在选民中引起共鸣。

latinEntries.structure: sonare, sono, sonavi, sonatum (v., first conjugation)

definition_zh: 放射性；放射性强度；放射现象；放射性污染
definition_en: the spontaneous emission of particles or rays from unstable atomic nuclei, or the strength of that emission
core_image: 一块看似安静的矿石放在暗处，计数器却持续作响，像有看不见的雨一直落下
scene: 实验室里，一块矿石让计数器持续作响。The sample's radioactivity fell by half in just over twelve days.
sceneCN: 这里 radioactivity 指「不稳定原子核自发放出粒子或射线的性质」（第 1 个义项：原子核自发辐射的现象）；句意：这个样品的放射性在十二天多一点后减半。图中可辨识物件：矿石、盖革计数器、铅屏蔽、记录纸。

forms.label: 罕用复数（指多种放射性现象）

senses.title: Spontaneous emission from unstable nuclei
senses.titleCN: 不稳定原子核的自发放射
senses.definition: the property of certain atomic nuclei to emit particles or rays without any outside trigger
senses.definitionCN: 某些原子核在无外界触发时自行放出粒子或射线的性质
senses.example: Radium's radioactivity was strong enough to fog a photographic plate.
senses.exampleCN: 镭的放射性强到足以使照相底片雾化。
senses.why: The name joins 'ray' to 'activity': the nucleus is active by sending out rays, and the word records exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字把「射线」与「活动」合起来：原子核靠发出射线而「活动」，词正记下这一点。

senses.title: The measured strength of a sample
senses.titleCN: 样品被测出的放射强度
senses.definition: the amount of radiation a particular material emits per unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 某种材料在单位时间内放出的辐射量
senses.example: The laboratory monitors the radioactivity of every waste drum.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室监测每一只废物桶的放射性强度。
senses.why: A property that can be strong or weak becomes a quantity, so the word also names the reading on the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 一种可强可弱的性质会变成可测的量，因此这个词也指仪器上的读数。

senses.title: The phenomenon and its study
senses.titleCN: 这种现象及其研究领域
senses.definition: the natural phenomenon discovered at the end of the nineteenth century, and the science built around it
senses.definitionCN: 十九世纪末发现的自然现象，以及围绕它建立的科学
senses.example: The discovery of radioactivity changed the idea of an immutable atom.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性的发现改变了原子不可变的观念。
senses.why: A newly found effect needs a name before it can become a discipline, and this word served both from the start.
senses.whyCN: 新发现的效应先要有名字才能成为学科，而这个词从一开始就兼顾两者。

senses.title: Radioactive contamination
senses.definition: radioactive material spread where it is not wanted, as on tools, soil or water
senses.definitionCN: 放射性物质扩散到不该出现的地方，如工具、土壤或水中
senses.example: Workers checked the drains for radioactivity after the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏之后，工人检查排水管是否带放射性。
senses.why: The abstract property stands in for the material that carries it, a common shift when a hazard is discussed.
senses.whyCN: 抽象性质被用来代替携带它的物质，这是讨论危险时常见的转喻。

senses.title: The tracer in medicine
senses.definition: the controlled use of radioactive substances to image or treat disease
senses.definitionCN: 有控制地利用放射性物质来成像或治疗疾病
senses.example: Doctors use radioactivity to see how a gland is working.
senses.exampleCN: 医生利用放射性来观察腺体的工作状况。
senses.why: Because emitted rays can be detected through the body, a harmless amount of the property becomes a diagnostic lamp.
senses.whyCN: 放出的射线能穿过身体被探测到，因此少量无害的放射性成了诊断之灯。

senses.title: The clock inside rocks
senses.definition: the use of decay rates as a natural clock for dating rocks and archaeological material
senses.definitionCN: 利用衰变速率作为天然时钟，为岩石与考古材料定年
senses.example: The team measured radioactivity to date the sediment.
senses.exampleCN: 团队测量放射性来确定沉积物的年代。
senses.why: Constant decay rates turn the property into a timer, because the remaining amount records how long it has been falling.
senses.whyCN: 恒定的衰变速率把这一性质变成计时器，因为剩余量记录了它已经下降了多久。

senses.title: The natural background level
senses.definition: the low level of radiation always present from soil, air, cosmic rays and living bodies
senses.definitionCN: 由土壤、空气、宇宙射线与生物体一直带来的低水平辐射
senses.example: The instrument first recorded the background radioactivity of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器先记录下房间的本底放射性。
senses.why: Any measurement needs a zero point, and the ever-present natural level supplies that baseline.
senses.whyCN: 任何测量都需要零点，而始终存在的天然水平提供了这个基线。

senses.title: Radioactivity made on purpose
senses.definition: radioactivity induced by bombarding stable nuclei with particles, first achieved in the 1930s
senses.definitionCN: 用粒子轰击稳定原子核而诱发的放射性，最早在二十世纪三十年代实现
senses.example: The pair produced artificial radioactivity by firing alpha particles at light nuclei.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位研究者用阿尔法粒子轰击轻核，造出了人工放射性。
senses.why: Once natural radioactivity was understood, making new unstable nuclei on demand became a distinct achievement needing its own label.
senses.whyCN: 天然放射性被理解之后，按需制造新的不稳定核成了一项独立成就，需要自己的名称。

intro.en: Radioactivity is a modern compound of Latin radius 'ray' and activus 'active'; the term was coined at the end of the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: radioactivity 是近代复合词，由拉丁 radius「射线」与 activus「活动的」构成；这个词在十九世纪末被造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Radius meant 'a staff, a spoke, a ray of light'. The spoke sense and the ray sense grew from the same straight line.
items.cn: radius 意为「杖、辐条、光线」。辐条义与光线义都从同一条直线引申而来。

items.en: Activus 'active' comes from agere 'to do, to drive', the verb behind agent, act and agenda.
items.cn: activus「活动的」出自 agere「做、驱动」，也就是 agent、act、agenda 背后的动词。

items.en: In the late 1890s newly found rays from uranium salts were described as a peculiar activity of the substance, and the word radioactivity followed.
items.cn: 十九世纪九十年代后期，铀盐新发现的射线被描述为物质的一种奇特活动，放射性一词随之出现。

items.en: Marie and Pierre Curie isolated radium and polonium and made radioactivity a measurable science rather than a curiosity.
items.cn: 居里夫妇分离出镭与钋，使放射性从奇观变成可测量的科学。

items.en: In the 1930s bombardment of light nuclei produced new unstable isotopes, and the phrase artificial radioactivity entered physics.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十年代轰击轻核产生了新的不稳定同位素，「人工放射性」进入物理学。

items.en: The exact first printing of the English term is approximate; the Latin components and the discovery period are well documented.
items.cn: 这个英语术语最早印行的确切年代为约数；拉丁构件与发现时期都有充分记录。

note.en: Group one holds ray-root and activity-root look-alikes; group two holds words for the radiation and the hazard itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「射线」或「活动」词根的形近词；第二组是辐射与危害本身的用词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a substance that emits radiation; radioactivity is the noun naming what it has.
entries.definitionCN: 描述会放出辐射的物质的形容词；而这个词是命名它所具性质的名词。

entries.definition: From the same ray-root but with an action ending: the rays themselves travelling outward, not the property of emitting them.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「射线」词根，但带动作结尾：指实际向外传播的射线，而非放出射线的性质。

entries.definition: The medical specialty that uses imaging, built on the same ray-root plus a word for study.
entries.definitionCN: 利用成像的医学专科，由同一「射线」词根加表示「学问」的成分构成。

entries.definition: From Latin radix 'root', not radius 'ray': it means going to the root, and only looks as if it belongs here.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「根」，而非「射线」：意为直抵根本，只是看起来像属于这一族。

entries.definition: The act of sending something out; it describes the event, while radioactivity names the lasting property.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物送出的动作；它描述事件，而这个词指持续的性质。

entries.definition: The nuclear process that produces the emission; radioactivity is what an observer measures because of it.
entries.definitionCN: 产生放射的核过程；而这个词是观察者因此测到的现象。

entries.definition: The unwanted presence of a dangerous substance; it can be radioactive or chemical, so it is wider than radioactivity.
entries.definitionCN: 危险物质不应有的存在；可以是放射性或化学的，因此比这个词更宽。

entries.definition: The time a sample needs to lose half its radioactivity; it measures the rate rather than the property.
entries.definitionCN: 样品失去一半放射性所需的时间；它衡量速率，而非性质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin radius 'ray' plus activus 'active': the activity of sending out rays.
normal.cn: 拉丁「射线」加「活动的」：发出射线的那种活动。

normal.en: The family runs radioactivity, radioactive, radioactively, radioisotope, radiogenic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括放射性、放射性的、以放射性的方式、放射性同位素、由衰变产生的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: natural radioactivity, artificial radioactivity, background radioactivity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：天然放射性、人工放射性、本底放射性。

normal.en: The ray-root appears in radiation and radiology, but radical comes from the word for root.
normal.cn: 「射线」词根出现在辐射与放射学里，而那个表示「根本的」形近词出自表示「根」的词。

normal.en: A Geiger counter turns radioactivity into clicks, which is how most people meet it.
normal.cn: 盖革计数器把放射性变成咔嗒声，多数人正是这样接触它。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet stone that keeps raining invisible particles into a detector.
abstract.cn: 想象一块安静的石头，持续向探测器落下看不见的粒子雨。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that never needs winding because the falling atoms are the pendulum.
abstract.cn: 想象一只不用上弦的钟，因为下落的原子就是摆。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that shines through flesh without being seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏穿过血肉却自身不可见的灯。

examples.en: The radioactivity of the soil was above the safety limit.
examples.cn: 这片土壤的放射性超过了安全限值。

examples.en: Natural radioactivity has always been part of the environment.
examples.cn: 天然放射性一直是环境的一部分。

examples.en: The hospital uses radioactivity to trace blood flow.
examples.cn: 医院利用放射性追踪血流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「radio（射线）+ activity（活动）」——不断放出射线的活动，就是放射性

root: 拉丁 radius「射线、辐条」+ activus「活动的」（出自 agere「做、驱动」）。英语 radioactivity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with spontaneous emission, then the measured level, the phenomenon, contamination, medical tracers, natural clocks, background radiation and finally radioactivity made on purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从自发放射开始，依次是测出的强度、现象本身、污染、医学示踪、天然时钟、本底辐射，最后是人为制造的放射性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quiet stone that keeps raining invisible particles, making a detector click without any visible cause.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块安静的石头持续落下看不见的粒子雨，使探测器无端作响。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND READING: the nucleus's own activity and the number on the instrument are the same fact before and after measurement.
branches.cn: 性质与读数：核自身的活动与仪器上的数字，是测量前后的同一事实。

branches.en: THE DISCOVERY: a new effect becomes a named phenomenon and then a science.
branches.cn: 发现：新效应先成为有名字的现象，再成为一门科学。

branches.en: THE SPREAD HAZARD: the property stands for the material that carries it into soil, water and tools.
branches.cn: 扩散的危险：性质被用来代替把它带进土壤、水源与工具的物质。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: the same emission becomes a lamp inside the body and a clock inside rock.
branches.cn: 器具：同一种放射既成为体内的灯，也成为岩石里的钟。

branches.en: THE BASELINE AND THE COPY: nature supplies a background level, and laboratories learn to make the effect themselves.
branches.cn: 基线与本制品：自然提供本底水平，实验室则学会自己制造这一效应。

intro.en: Radioactivity joins a Latin word for ray to a Latin-derived word for activity, a pattern typical of nineteenth-century science.
intro.cn: radioactivity 把拉丁语的「射线」接到由拉丁语派生的「活动」上，这是十九世纪科学命名的典型模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius yields radius, radial, radiate and radiation; agere yields act, active, agent and agenda.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 radius 衍生 radius、radial、radiate、radiation；agere 衍生 act、active、agent、agenda。

items.meaning: a spoke, a staff, a ray
items.example: The same word names a wheel spoke and a light ray.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词既指车轮辐条，也指光线。

items.example: The prefix marks rays emitted or received.
items.exampleCN: 这个构词成分标出发出或接收的射线。

items.structure: agere (Latin verb, third conjugation, 'to do, drive')
items.example: The verb supplies the idea of being at work.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「正在起作用」的意思。

items.example: An active substance works on its own.
items.exampleCN: 活性物质会自行起作用。

items.meaning: the state of being at work
items.example: The activity of the sample was recorded hourly.
items.exampleCN: 样品的活动状态每小时被记录一次。

items.meaning: the emission of rays by nuclei
items.example: Radium's radioactivity was soon measurable.
items.exampleCN: 镭的放射性很快就可测量了。

items.example: The isotope is radioactive for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这种同位素会在数百年间保持放射性。

items.example: The shield blocked most of the radiation.
items.exampleCN: 屏蔽挡住了大部分辐射。

latinEntries.meaning: a spoke, a staff, a ray

latinEntries.structure: agere, ago, egi, actum (v., third conjugation)

definition_zh: 放射性衰变；不稳定原子核自发转变为另一种核并放出辐射的过程
definition_en: the spontaneous transformation of an unstable atomic nucleus into another nucleus, accompanied by the emission of particles or rays
core_image: 一排灯逐盏熄灭，每灭一盏就留下一点余热，而熄灭的节奏始终不变
scene: 探测器旁的样品每发生一次衰变，计数就增加一格。Every radioactive decay in the sample added one more count to the detector.
sceneCN: 这里 radioactive decay 指「不稳定核自发转变并放出辐射的过程」（第 1 个义项：原子核自发改变化学身份的过程）；句意：样品中每一次放射性衰变，都让探测器的计数增加一格。图中可辨识物件：样品盒、探测器、计数刻度、屏蔽层。

pos.zh: 放射性衰变（可数或不可数）

senses.title: The nuclear transformation itself
senses.titleCN: 原子核自身的转变过程
senses.definition: the process by which an unstable nucleus changes into a different nucleus and emits radiation
senses.definitionCN: 不稳定原子核变成另一种原子核并放出辐射的过程
senses.example: Radioactive decay turns uranium into a long series of lighter nuclei.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性衰变把铀变成一长串更轻的核。
senses.why: Decay here keeps the old image of falling away, applied to a nucleus that cannot hold its present form.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「衰」保留了旧有的「落下、消减」意象，只是用在了一个维持不住现有形态的原子核上。

senses.title: A single decay event
senses.definition: one individual act of transformation by one nucleus at one moment
senses.definitionCN: 某一个原子核在某一时刻发生的一次转变
senses.example: Each radioactive decay releases a fixed amount of energy.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次放射性衰变都放出固定数量的能量。
senses.why: The process is countable at the level of single nuclei, so the same phrase names one event as well as the whole phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程在单个核的层面可数，因此同一短语既指整体现象，也指一次事件。

senses.title: The rate and the half-life
senses.definition: the predictable speed at which a sample decays, expressed as a half-life
senses.definitionCN: 样品衰变的可预测速度，以半衰期表示
senses.example: The rate of radioactive decay does not change with temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性衰变的速率不随温度改变。
senses.why: Because each nucleus decays at random but the population follows a fixed curve, the rate became the measurable face of the process.
senses.whyCN: 单个核的衰变随机，整体却遵循固定曲线，因此速率成了这个过程可测量的一面。

senses.title: A particular mode of decay
senses.definition: one of the routes a nucleus can take, such as alpha, beta or gamma emission
senses.definitionCN: 原子核可走的某条路径，如放出阿尔法、贝塔或伽马射线
senses.example: Beta decay changes a neutron into a proton inside the nucleus.
senses.exampleCN: 贝塔衰变使核内的一个中子变成一个质子。
senses.why: Different nuclei fall apart in different ways, and each route is called a mode of the same general process.
senses.whyCN: 不同的核以不同方式解体，每条路径都称为同一总过程的某种模式。

senses.title: A chain of successive decays
senses.definition: a series in which each decay product is itself unstable and decays in turn
senses.definitionCN: 每一个衰变产物自身也不稳定、继续衰变的序列
senses.example: The decay chain ends only when a stable lead isotope is reached.
senses.exampleCN: 这条衰变链直到抵达稳定的铅同位素才结束。
senses.why: One fall makes the next possible, so the process is naturally described as a chain rather than a single step.
senses.whyCN: 一次下落使下一次成为可能，因此这个过程天然被描述成链，而不是单步。

senses.title: The natural clock for dating
senses.definition: the use of a known decay rate to calculate the age of a rock or a once-living object
senses.definitionCN: 利用已知衰变速率计算岩石或曾存活物体的年龄
senses.example: Carbon dating depends on the radioactive decay of a rare isotope.
senses.exampleCN: 碳定年依赖一种稀有同位素的放射性衰变。
senses.why: A constant rate turns the remaining amount into a record of elapsed time, so the process doubles as a clock.
senses.whyCN: 恒定的速率使剩余量成为流逝时间的记录，因此这个过程兼作时钟。

senses.title: Heat from falling nuclei
senses.definition: the warmth produced inside the Earth or a waste container by ongoing decay
senses.definitionCN: 地球内部或废物容器中因持续衰变而产生的热
senses.example: Radioactive decay keeps the planet's interior warm.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性衰变使行星内部保持温热。
senses.why: Each decay releases energy that becomes heat, so the process is also an internal furnace.
senses.whyCN: 每次衰变都放出会变成热的能量，因此这个过程也是一座内部熔炉。

senses.title: The counted signature in a detector
senses.titleCN: 探测器里被计数的信号
senses.definition: the individual clicks or counts by which an instrument records that decay is happening
senses.definitionCN: 仪器借以记录衰变正在发生的单次咔嗒或计数
senses.example: The detector logged one radioactive decay every few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器每隔几秒就记录到一次放射性衰变。
senses.why: What an instrument can actually see is a count, so the abstract process is also named by its smallest observable sign.
senses.whyCN: 仪器真正能看到的只是一次计数，因此这个抽象过程也用它最小的可观测迹象来称呼。

intro.en: Radioactive decay combines the ray-and-activity compound with decay, from Latin decadere 'to fall away'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: radioactive decay 把「射线—活动」复合词与 decay 结合，而 decay 出自拉丁 decadere「落下、消减」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cadere meant 'to fall', and it supplies the falling image in decay, accident and cadence.
items.cn: cadere 意为「落下」，为 decay、accident、cadence 提供了「下落」的意象。

items.en: De- 'down, away' plus cadere produced decadere, 'to fall away, to sink', the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 「向下、离开」加「落下」构成 decadere，意为「落走、下沉」，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French decair carried the word into English, where it first described rotting matter or declining fortunes.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带进英语，最初描述腐烂之物或衰败的境遇。

items.en: When unstable nuclei were found to change spontaneously, the old word for falling away described the change without implying any outside cause.
items.cn: 当不稳定核被发现会自行变化时，这个表示「落走」的旧词正好描述这种变化，且不暗示任何外因。

items.en: Twentieth-century geology added decay chains, decay heat and decay products as the process became a tool and a heat source.
items.cn: 二十世纪的地质学又添了衰变链、衰变热与衰变产物，这个过程成了工具与热源。

items.en: The first written uses of the exact phrase are approximate; the Latin chain is well attested.
items.cn: 这个确切短语最早的书证年代为约数；拉丁语链条有充分记录。

note.en: Group one holds fall-root words and one term that only looks related; group two holds words for the splitting and the timing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「落下」词根的词与一个只是看起来相关的术语；第二组是关于分裂与计时的词。

entries.definition: The bare verb or noun for falling away, used of teeth, buildings and nuclei alike; the physics phrase narrows it to nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 表示落下、消减的动词或名词，可用于牙齿、建筑与原子核；物理短语把它收窄到核。

entries.definition: From the same falling-away stock: a decline in standards or morals, with no physics involved.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「落走」词源：指标准或道德的衰退，与物理无关。

entries.definition: Built on the same falling verb: trees whose leaves fall each year, a literal use of the old image.
entries.definitionCN: 构于同一个「落下」动词：指每年落叶的树，是旧意象的字面用法。

entries.definition: Probably from Dutch or another source meaning a lure; it is not related to the falling root despite the shared opening.
entries.definitionCN: 可能来自荷兰语或其他表示「诱饵」的来源；尽管开头相同，与「落下」词根无关。

entries.definition: The splitting of a heavy nucleus into two large parts; it is one kind of nuclear change, often triggered rather than spontaneous.
entries.definitionCN: 重核裂成两个较大部分；它是核变化的一种，常被触发而非自发。

entries.definition: The historical word for one element changing into another, which radioactive decay achieves naturally.
entries.definitionCN: 一种元素变成另一种的旧称，而放射性衰变正是自然实现这一点的方式。

entries.definition: The time needed for half a sample to decay; it is a measure of the process, not the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 样品一半发生衰变所需的时间；它衡量过程，而非过程本身。

entries.definition: A general word for falling into pieces; early physics used it for decay, but it is wider and less precise.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指碎成小块；早期物理学用它指衰变，但它更宽泛也更不精确。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: radioactive 'ray-active' plus decay 'fall away': nuclei falling away while sending out rays.
normal.cn: 「射线活动的」加「落走」：原子核一边落走一边发出射线。

normal.en: The family runs decay, decayed, decay product, decay series, radioactive decay.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括衰变、已衰变的、衰变产物、衰变系列、放射性衰变。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: rate of decay, decay chain, decay heat.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：衰变速率、衰变链、衰变热。

normal.en: The same falling root appears in decadence and deciduous, both literal or social falls.
normal.cn: 同一个「落下」词根出现在「衰败」与「落叶」这两个词里，一个是社会下落，一个是字面落下。

normal.en: Half-life turns the process into a clock, which is why rocks can be dated.
normal.cn: 半衰期把过程变成时钟，岩石因此可以被定年。

abstract.en: Picture a row of lamps going out one by one at a rhythm that never changes.
abstract.cn: 想象一排灯以始终不变的节奏一盏盏熄灭。

abstract.en: Picture a falling stone that leaves a little warmth each time it lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一块下落的石头，每次落地都留下一点余温。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose pendulum is a nucleus and whose ticks are clicks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，摆是原子核，滴答是计数器的咔嗒。

examples.en: Radioactive decay is unaffected by ordinary heat or pressure.
examples.cn: 放射性衰变不受普通温度或压力的影响。

examples.en: The decay chain of uranium ends in a stable isotope of lead.
examples.cn: 铀的衰变链最终止于一种稳定的铅同位素。

examples.en: Geologists date the layer by measuring radioactive decay.
examples.cn: 地质学家通过测量放射性衰变来确定这一层的年代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「radioactive（放射性的）+ decay（衰败）」——一边放出射线一边衰下去，就是放射性衰变

root: radioactive（radius「射线」+ activus「活动的」）+ decay（拉丁 decadere「落走」= de-「向下」+ cadere「落下」）。英语 radioactive decay。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a nucleus falling away: the whole process, one event, its rate, its modes, its chain, its use as a clock, its heat and the single click a detector records.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一个落走的核展开：整个过程、一次事件、速率、方式、链条、作为时钟、作为热源，以及探测器记下的一次咔嗒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp after another going out at a fixed rhythm, each leaving a trace of warmth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排灯以固定节奏逐盏熄灭，每一盏都留下一点温热。

branches.en: PROCESS AND INSTANCE: the long transformation and a single nucleus's turn are the same fall at two magnifications.
branches.cn: 过程与单例：漫长的转变与某一个核的一次变化，是同一次下落的两种放大。

branches.en: THE METRONOME: random individual events add up to a fixed rate, and that rate becomes measurable.
branches.cn: 节拍器：单个事件随机，合起来却是固定速率，而这一速率变得可测。

branches.en: THE ROUTES: different nuclei take different paths, and each path leaves a product that may fall again.
branches.cn: 路径：不同的核走不同的路，每条路都留下可能再次下落的产物。

branches.en: THE TWO USES: the constant rate reads as elapsed time in rock, and as warmth in the Earth.
branches.cn: 两种用途：恒定速率在岩石里读作流逝的时间，在地球里读作温热。

branches.en: THE OBSERVABLE SIGN: what a detector can actually record is one click at a time.
branches.cn: 可观测的迹象：探测器真正能记录的，只是一次一次的咔嗒。

intro.en: The phrase joins a modern science compound to an old verb of falling, so one half is nineteenth-century and the other is Latin.
intro.cn: 这个短语把近代科学复合词接到一个古老的「落下」动词上，一半是十九世纪，一半是拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius and agere form the first word; Latin cadere and its compound decadere form the second, and cadere also yields accident, cadence and case.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 radius 与 agere 构成第一个词；拉丁 cadere 及其复合形式 decadere 构成第二个词，cadere 还衍生出 accident、cadence、case。

items.example: The ray-root begins the physics word.
items.exampleCN: 「射线」词根开启了这个物理词。

items.example: The adjective says the nucleus is at work.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词说明原子核正在运作。

items.example: The verb supplies the falling image.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供下落的意象。

items.example: The prefix directs the fall downward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把下落引向下方。

items.example: The compound gave English decay.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式给英语提供了表示「衰败」的动词。

items.example: Wood decays faster in damp air.
items.exampleCN: 木头在潮湿空气里腐烂得更快。

items.meaning: the nucleus left after a decay
items.example: The decay product is often unstable too.
items.exampleCN: 衰变产物往往也不稳定。

items.example: The critics spoke of cultural decadence.
items.exampleCN: 批评者谈到文化的衰败。

latinEntries.structure: cadere, cado, cecidi, casum (v., third conjugation)

definition_zh: 核能；原子核释放的能量；核能发电；核工业
definition_en: energy released from atomic nuclei, especially as electricity generated by nuclear reactors
core_image: 一颗极小的核被打开或合并，放出的热把一整片水变成蒸汽，蒸汽再推动巨大的叶片
scene: 这个国家的电表里，有三分之一来自原子核。The country now draws a third of its electricity from nuclear energy.
sceneCN: 这里 nuclear energy 指「原子核释放并被用来发电的能量」（第 1 个义项：核裂变或核聚变释放的能量）；句意：这个国家如今有三分之一的电力来自核能。图中可辨识物件：反应堆厂房、冷却塔、电网、仪表盘。

senses.title: Energy released from atomic nuclei
senses.definition: the energy set free when heavy nuclei split or light nuclei combine
senses.definitionCN: 重核裂开或轻核结合时释放出来的能量
senses.example: A gram of uranium yields more nuclear energy than a tonne of coal.
senses.exampleCN: 一克铀释放的核能超过一吨煤。
senses.why: The nucleus holds its parts together with enormous force, and releasing those parts releases the energy that kept them bound.
senses.whyCN: 原子核以极大的力把各部分束缚在一起，松开这些部分便放出原本维系它们的能量。

senses.title: Electricity from reactors
senses.definition: the electrical power produced when reactor heat drives turbines
senses.definitionCN: 反应堆的热驱动汽轮机所产生的电力
senses.example: Nuclear energy supplies a large share of the grid at night.
senses.exampleCN: 核能在夜间为电网提供很大一部分电力。
senses.why: Heat from fission is turned into steam and then into current, so the phrase also names the product at the socket.
senses.whyCN: 裂变产生的热先变成蒸汽再变成电流，因此这个短语也指插座上的那个产品。

senses.title: The industry and its policy
senses.definition: the sector of companies, regulators and programmes that build and run nuclear plants
senses.definitionCN: 建造与运营核电站的企业、监管机构与计划所构成的部门
senses.example: The debate over nuclear energy divides the parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 围绕核能的争论使议会分裂。
senses.why: An energy source that requires huge capital becomes an institution, and the phrase shifts from physics to politics.
senses.whyCN: 一种需要巨额资本的能源会成为制度，于是这个短语从物理滑向政治。

senses.title: The binding energy inside the nucleus
senses.definition: the energy stored in the bonds between nucleons, measurable as the mass the nucleus lacks
senses.definitionCN: 储存在核子之间、可通过核所缺的质量测出的能量
senses.example: The binding energy of iron is at the peak of the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 铁的结合能正处在曲线的顶点。
senses.why: Mass and energy are interchangeable, and the missing mass of a nucleus is exactly the nuclear energy that would be needed to take it apart.
senses.whyCN: 质量与能量可以互换，而核所缺的那部分质量，正是把它拆开所需的核能。

senses.title: The energy of a nuclear weapon
senses.definition: the explosive energy released by an uncontrolled fission or fusion reaction
senses.definitionCN: 不受控的裂变或聚变反应放出的爆炸能量
senses.example: The first test proved that nuclear energy could be released in an instant.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次试验证明核能可以在一瞬间释放。
senses.why: The same binding energy, released slowly in a reactor, becomes a blast when released at once.
senses.whyCN: 同样的结合能，在反应堆里缓慢释放便是电力，一次性释放便成爆炸。

senses.title: The power that lights the stars
senses.definition: the energy produced by fusion inside stars, including the sun
senses.definitionCN: 恒星内部、包括太阳内部由聚变产生的能量
senses.example: All sunlight is nuclear energy arriving from the core.
senses.exampleCN: 所有阳光都是来自太阳核心的核能。
senses.why: Stars run on the same nuclear reactions, so the phrase names the source of daylight as well as of electricity.
senses.whyCN: 恒星靠同样的核反应运转，因此这个短语既指日光的来源，也指电力的来源。

senses.title: The older name for the same thing
senses.definition: the historical label atomic energy, used before the nucleus was understood as the source
senses.definitionCN: 历史上的「原子能」说法，在人们弄清能量源于原子核之前使用
senses.example: Old textbooks speak of atomic energy where new ones say nuclear energy.
senses.exampleCN: 旧教科书说「原子能」，新教科书则说「核能」。
senses.why: The atom was the known unit when the effect was discovered, so the older name credited the whole atom rather than its centre.
senses.whyCN: 发现这一效应时，原子是已知的单位，因此旧名把功劳记在整个原子上，而不是它的中心。

senses.title: The heat inside the Earth
senses.definition: the geothermal heat produced by the decay of radioactive isotopes in the planet's interior
senses.definitionCN: 行星内部放射性同位素衰变所产生的地热
senses.example: Nuclear energy keeps the mantle warm enough to move.
senses.exampleCN: 核能使地幔保持足以流动的温热。
senses.why: Decay releases energy continuously, and over billions of years that trickle has become a planetary furnace.
senses.whyCN: 衰变持续放出能量，数十亿年下来，这点滴之热成了一座行星熔炉。

intro.en: Nuclear energy joins nuclear, from Latin nucleus 'kernel, nut', to energy, from Greek energeia 'activity'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nuclear energy 把源于拉丁 nucleus「果仁、核」的 nuclear 接到源于希腊 energeia「活动」的 energy 上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nux, nucis meant 'nut'. The small hard kernel inside supplied the image of a compact centre.
items.cn: nux 意为「坚果」。里面那颗小而硬的仁，提供了「紧密中心」的意象。

items.en: The diminutive nucleus meant 'a little nut, a kernel', and Latin writers already used it for the core of a thing.
items.cn: 指小形式 nucleus 意为「小坚果、果仁」，拉丁作者已用它指某物的核心。

items.en: Energeia meant 'activity, working', built from en 'in' and ergon 'work'. Latin borrowed it as energia.
items.cn: energeia 意为「活动、运作」，由「在内」与「工作」构成。拉丁语借入为 energia。

items.en: As the cell nucleus and later the atomic nucleus were named, the kernel image moved from biology to physics.
items.cn: 随着细胞核、后来又随原子核被命名，果仁的意象从生物学移到了物理学。

items.en: The phrase nuclear energy spread as reactors and weapons showed that the nucleus stores vast energy.
items.cn: 反应堆与武器显示核内储存巨大能量之后，「核能」这一说法传播开来。

items.en: The first uses of the exact phrase are approximate; both source words are fully attested.
items.cn: 这个确切短语最早的使用年代为约数；两个来源词都有完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds nut-root look-alikes; group two holds names for the same energy measured in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「坚果」词根的形近词；第二组是从其他角度称呼同一种能量的说法。

entries.definition: The bare adjective meaning 'of the nucleus'; it describes weapons, reactors and medicine as well as energy.
entries.definitionCN: 指「原子核的」的形容词；它除能量外也修饰武器、反应堆与医学。

entries.definition: The central body of an atom or cell; the energy is named after the object that stores it.
entries.definitionCN: 原子或细胞的核心体；能量以储存它的那个对象命名。

entries.definition: From the same kernel-root: relating to the nucleus of a cell, as in nucleic acid, with no connection to reactors.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「核」词根：指细胞核的，如核酸，与反应堆无关。

entries.definition: The everyday English word from the same ancient root; the scientific nucleus began as a little nut.
entries.definitionCN: 与那个古老词根同源的日常英语词；科学上的「核」原本就是一颗小坚果。

entries.definition: The pre-1940s label for the same power; it credited the whole atom before the nucleus was known to be the source.
entries.definitionCN: 二十世纪四十年代以前对同一种动力的称呼；在弄清核才是来源之前，它把功劳记在整个原子。

entries.definition: Usually the electrical output or the industry; nuclear energy is the broader physical and political term.
entries.definitionCN: 通常指电力产出或这个行业；而「核能」这一说法则是更宽泛的物理与政治用语。

entries.definition: The precise measure of the energy that holds a nucleus together; it explains where nuclear energy comes from.
entries.definitionCN: 维系原子核的能量之精确度量；它解释了核能从哪里来。

entries.definition: The spontaneous emission of rays; it is one route by which nuclear energy appears as heat.
entries.definitionCN: 自发放出的射线；它是核能以热的形式出现的一条途径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin nucleus 'kernel' plus Greek energeia 'activity': the activity of the kernel.
normal.cn: 拉丁「果仁」加希腊「活动」：果仁的活动。

normal.en: The family runs nuclear energy, nuclear, nuclear power, nuclear reactor, nuclear-free.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括核能、核的、核电、核反应堆、无核的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: nuclear energy plant, nuclear energy policy, civil nuclear energy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：核能电站、核能政策、民用核能。

normal.en: The old name atomic energy credited the whole atom; the new name credits its kernel.
normal.cn: 旧名「原子能」把功劳记在整个原子，新名则记在它的果仁。

normal.en: The same binding energy is slow heat in a reactor and instant blast in a weapon.
normal.cn: 同一份结合能，在反应堆里是缓慢的热，在武器里是一瞬的爆。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny stone that can boil an entire lake.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小石头能烧开整片湖。

abstract.en: Picture a nut whose shell holds a whole winter of warmth.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗果壳里装着整个冬天的暖。

abstract.en: Picture a star and a power station lit by the same small fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗恒星与一座电站由同一点小火点亮。

examples.en: Nuclear energy produces no carbon dioxide while running.
examples.cn: 核能在运行时不产生二氧化碳。

examples.en: The country expanded nuclear energy after the oil crisis.
examples.cn: 石油危机之后，这个国家扩大了核能。

examples.en: Some of the Earth's internal heat is nuclear energy from decaying isotopes.
examples.cn: 地球内部的一部分热来自同位素衰变产生的核能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nuclear（核的）+ energy（能量）」——原子核里放出的能量，就是核能

root: nuclear（拉丁 nucleus「果仁、核」，为 nux「坚果」的指小形式）+ energy（希腊 energeia「活动」= en「在内」+ ergon「工作」）。英语 nuclear energy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the released binding energy to the electricity, the industry, the stored quantity itself, the weapon, the star, the older name and finally the planet's internal heat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从释放的结合能走到电力、行业、被储存的量本身、武器、恒星、旧称，最后是行星内部的热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kernel opened or joined, and its heat turning water into steam that drives great blades.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗核被打开或合并，它的热把水变成蒸汽，蒸汽推动巨大的叶片。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: the energy released and the energy stored are the same quantity before and after the bond is broken.
branches.cn: 来源：被放出的能量与被储存的能量，是键被打开前后的同一个量。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: heat becomes current, and current becomes an industry with rules and budgets.
branches.cn: 体系：热变成电流，电流又变成一个带规则与预算的行业。

branches.en: THE TWO EXTREMES: released at once it is a blast, released steadily in a star it is daylight.
branches.cn: 两个极端：一次性放出是爆炸，在恒星里稳定放出则是日光。

branches.en: THE OLD LABEL: the earlier name credited the whole atom before the kernel was understood.
branches.cn: 旧标签：早先的名字在弄清核之前把功劳记在整个原子。

branches.en: THE DEEP FURNACE: the slow decay of isotopes keeps the planet's interior warm.
branches.cn: 深处熔炉：同位素的缓慢衰变使行星内部保持温热。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin kernel word with a Greek word for working, a typical scientific mixture.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的「果仁」与希腊语的「运作」配对，是典型的科学混合造词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nucleus and nux also yield nuclear, nucleic and nut; Greek energeia came into Latin as energia and then into English as energy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nucleus 与 nux 还衍生出 nuclear、nucleic 与 nut；希腊 energeia 进入拉丁语成为 energia，再进入英语成为 energy。

items.example: The hard shell protects a small kernel.
items.exampleCN: 硬壳保护着里面的小仁。

items.example: The diminutive names the core of a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个指小形式指某物的核心。

items.example: Nuclear forces hold the protons together.
items.exampleCN: 核力把质子维系在一起。

items.example: Nucleic acids carry inherited information.
items.exampleCN: 核酸携带遗传信息。

items.example: The word names work being done.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指正在被做的工作。

items.example: Energy is stored in the bonds of the nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 能量储存在原子核的键里。

items.example: Nuclear energy is released in reactors.
items.exampleCN: 核能在反应堆中被释放。

items.example: The reactor turns heat into steam.
items.exampleCN: 反应堆把热变成蒸汽。

latinEntries.structure: energia, energiae (f., first declension, from Greek energeia)

definition_zh: 核聚变；轻原子核结合成较重原子核并释放能量的过程
definition_en: the process in which two light atomic nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
core_image: 两粒很小的核被极高的热逼到一起，合为一粒更大的核，同时放出一束光
scene: 太阳核心把氢变成氦，光与热就这样产生。Nuclear fusion in the sun's core turns hydrogen into helium.
