sceneCN: 这里 nuclear fusion 指「轻核结合成较重核并释放能量」（第 1 个义项：轻原子核合并的核反应过程）；句意：太阳核心的核聚变把氢变成氦。图中可辨识物件：太阳剖面、核心区、氢核、氦核。

senses.title: Light nuclei joining into a heavier one
senses.definition: the nuclear reaction in which two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 两个轻原子核结合成一个较重原子核的核反应
senses.example: Deuterium and tritium are the easiest fuels for nuclear fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 氘与氚是核聚变最容易使用的燃料。
senses.why: Latin fusion means 'a pouring together', and the two nuclei are literally poured into one larger body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义是「倒在一起」，两粒核确实被倒进一个更大的身体里。

senses.title: The power source of stars
senses.definition: the fusion reactions in stellar cores that keep stars shining for billions of years
senses.definitionCN: 恒星核心中使恒星发光数十亿年的聚变反应
senses.example: Without nuclear fusion the sun would collapse within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 没有核聚变，太阳会在数小时内坍缩。
senses.why: Gravity squeezes the core until hydrogen nuclei merge, and the released energy balances the squeeze.
senses.whyCN: 引力把核心压到氢核合并，放出的能量又抵住这份挤压。

senses.title: The laboratory attempt to hold a plasma
senses.titleCN: 实验室里约束等离子体的尝试
senses.definition: research that confines a hot ionized gas long enough for fusion to occur
senses.definitionCN: 把高温电离气体约束足够久、使聚变得以发生的研究
senses.example: Magnetic fields are used to keep the plasma away from the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 磁场被用来让等离子体远离器壁。
senses.why: Fusion needs temperatures above the sun's core, so the central problem is containment rather than fuel.
senses.whyCN: 聚变需要高于太阳核心的温度，因此核心难题是约束，而不是燃料。

senses.title: The fusion power plant
senses.definition: an engineered reactor designed to produce useful heat from fusion, such as a tokamak
senses.definitionCN: 为从聚变获得可用热量而设计的工程反应堆，如托卡马克
senses.example: The tokamak is the most developed nuclear fusion design.
senses.exampleCN: 托卡马克是最成熟的核聚变设计。
senses.why: Once the physics is understood, the phrase names the machine that would turn it into power.
senses.whyCN: 物理被理解之后，这个短语便指那台将把它变成电力的机器。

senses.title: The thermonuclear weapon
senses.definition: an uncontrolled fusion reaction ignited by a fission explosion
senses.definitionCN: 由裂变爆炸点燃的不受控聚变反应
senses.example: A hydrogen bomb relies on nuclear fusion for most of its yield.
senses.exampleCN: 氢弹的大部分当量来自核聚变。
senses.why: Fusion releases far more energy per unit mass, so weapons use it as a second, larger stage.
senses.whyCN: 聚变每单位质量放出的能量多得多，因此武器把它用作更大的一级。

senses.title: Net energy gain
senses.definition: the condition in which a fusion reaction returns more energy than was spent heating and confining it
senses.definitionCN: 聚变反应放出的能量超过用于加热与约束的能量
senses.example: The experiment finally reached net energy gain from nuclear fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这次实验终于实现了核聚变的净能量增益。
senses.why: A power source is only useful if it pays back its own running cost, so breaking even became a milestone with its own phrase.
senses.whyCN: 一种能源只有偿还自身运行成本才有用，因此「收支相抵」成了有专门说法的一座里程碑。

senses.title: The disputed tabletop claim
senses.titleCN: 有争议的台面聚变说法
senses.definition: the 1989 claim that fusion could occur in simple room-temperature cells, which was not reproduced
senses.definitionCN: 1989 年声称聚变可在简单的室温装置中发生，但未能被重复
senses.example: Cold fusion was announced as nuclear fusion at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 「冷聚变」曾被宣布为室温下的核聚变。
senses.why: The claim borrowed the prestige of fusion while skipping the extreme conditions, which is why the term still carries doubt.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法借用了聚变的声望，却跳过了极端条件，因此该术语至今带着疑问。

senses.title: The helium ash that must be removed
senses.definition: the helium produced by fusion, which must be exhausted so that it does not dilute the fuel
senses.definitionCN: 聚变产生的氦，必须排出，以免稀释燃料
senses.example: The reactor must pump out the helium ash from nuclear fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 反应堆必须把核聚变产生的氦灰抽走。
senses.why: A furnace that keeps its own ashes will smother, so the product of fusion becomes an engineering problem with a name.
senses.whyCN: 留着自身灰烬的炉子会闷灭，因此聚变的产物成了一个有名字的工程问题。

intro.en: Nuclear fusion joins the Latin kernel word to Latin fusio 'a pouring', from fundere 'to pour, to melt'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nuclear fusion 把拉丁语的「果仁」接到拉丁 fusio「倾倒」上，而 fusio 出自 fundere「倒、熔」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fundere meant 'to pour, to melt, to cast', and it produced the image of separate things flowing into one.
items.cn: fundere 意为「倒、熔、铸」，造出了分开之物流成一体的意象。

items.en: Fusio named a pouring or a melting, the act that turns separate pieces into a single mass.
items.cn: fusio 指倾倒或熔合，是把分开的块变成一整团的动作。

items.en: English borrowed fusion for melting and for the joining of things, long before it meant a nuclear reaction.
items.cn: 英语借入 fusion 指熔化与结合，远在它指核反应之前。

items.en: Twentieth-century physics explained starlight as the fusion of hydrogen into helium, and the word moved to the nucleus.
items.cn: 二十世纪物理学把星光解释为氢聚变成氦，这个词于是移到了原子核上。

items.en: Controlled fusion research added fusion reactor, plasma confinement and net gain to the vocabulary.
items.cn: 受控聚变研究又为词汇添了聚变堆、等离子体约束与净增益。

items.en: The first uses of the exact phrase are approximate; the Latin chain is fully recorded.
items.cn: 这个确切短语最早的使用年代为约数；拉丁语链条有完整记录。

note.en: Group one holds pour-root look-alikes and one near-twin from a splitting root; group two holds words for joining and for the rival reaction.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「倾倒」词根的形近词，外加一个来自「分裂」词根的近形词；第二组是表示结合与竞争反应的说法。

entries.definition: The general word for melting or joining, also used of cuisine and music; the nuclear phrase narrows it to nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指熔化或结合，也用于烹饪与音乐；核短语把它收窄到原子核。

entries.definition: To melt together, or the safety device that melts to break a circuit; both keep the pouring-and-melting image.
entries.definitionCN: 熔合，或熔断以断开电路的安全装置；两者都保留「倾倒与熔化」的意象。

entries.definition: From Latin findere 'to split': a crack or a cleft, close in shape to fusion but opposite in image.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「分裂」：指裂缝或裂口，形状接近但意象相反。

entries.definition: Latin con- 'together' plus fundere 'pour': to pour things together until they cannot be told apart.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁「共同」加「倒」：把东西倒在一起，直到分不清。

entries.definition: The splitting of a heavy nucleus; it releases energy in the opposite direction from fusion.
entries.definitionCN: 重核裂开；它从相反方向释放能量，与聚变相对。

entries.definition: Describing fusion driven by very high temperature, as in stars and hydrogen bombs.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由极高温驱动的聚变，如恒星与氢弹中的情形。

entries.definition: The general word for two bodies becoming one; it carries no nuclear meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指两个实体合而为一；不含核物理含义。

entries.definition: Greek 'a putting together': the building of a whole from parts, often chemical rather than nuclear.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「放在一起」：由部分组成整体，常指化学而非核过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin nucleus 'kernel' plus fusio 'a pouring': two kernels poured into one.
normal.cn: 拉丁「果仁」加「倾倒」：两粒仁被倒成一粒。

normal.en: The family runs nuclear fusion, fusion, fusion reactor, thermonuclear.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括核聚变、聚变、聚变堆、热核的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: controlled nuclear fusion, nuclear fusion research, nuclear fusion power.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：受控核聚变、核聚变研究、聚变能。

normal.en: Fusion and fission are opposites: one pours together, the other splits apart.
normal.cn: 聚变与裂变相反：一个倒在一起，一个裂开。

normal.en: The sun is the oldest working fusion reactor, and it needs no containment.
normal.cn: 太阳是最古老的运转中的聚变堆，而且不需要约束装置。

abstract.en: Picture two small flames pressed into one larger flame.
abstract.cn: 想象两簇小火被压成一簇更大的火。

abstract.en: Picture a furnace that must also sweep away its own ashes.
abstract.cn: 想象一座还得扫掉自身灰烬的炉子。

abstract.en: Picture a star held up by the very fire it is making.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗恒星被自己造出的火撑住。

examples.en: Nuclear fusion requires temperatures of millions of degrees.
examples.cn: 核聚变需要数百万度的温度。

examples.en: The sun's nuclear fusion has run for billions of years.
examples.cn: 太阳的核聚变已经运行了数十亿年。

examples.en: Engineers still cannot sustain nuclear fusion for long periods.
examples.cn: 工程师仍无法长时间维持核聚变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nuclear（核的）+ fusion（融合）」——核与核融在一起，就是核聚变

root: nuclear（拉丁 nucleus「果仁、核」）+ fusion（拉丁 fusio「倾倒」← fundere「倒、熔」）。英语 nuclear fusion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow two nuclei joining: the reaction, the star, the laboratory plasma, the power plant, the weapon, net gain, the disputed cold claim and the helium ash left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着两粒核的结合展开：反应本身、恒星、实验室等离子体、发电装置、武器、净增益、有争议的冷聚变说法，以及留下的氦灰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two tiny kernels forced together by heat, becoming one larger kernel and releasing a flash.
core.cn: 核心意象：两粒小核被热逼到一起，合成一粒更大的核，并放出一道闪光。

branches.en: THE REACTION: the laboratory description and the stellar furnace are the same joining at two scales.
branches.cn: 反应：实验室的描述与恒星熔炉，是同一结合的两个尺度。

branches.en: THE CONTAINMENT: research holds a plasma, and engineering designs the reactor around that hold.
branches.cn: 约束：研究把等离子体困住，工程则围绕这个「困住」设计反应堆。

branches.en: THE EXTREMES: released at once it is a weapon, released profitably it must return more than it costs.
branches.cn: 两个极端：一次性释放是武器，要有利可图则须产出大于投入。

branches.en: THE SHORT CUT: a claim tried to skip the heat, and the doubt is part of the word's history.
branches.cn: 捷径：有人试图跳过高温，疑问于是成了这个词历史的一部分。

branches.en: THE RESIDUE: the helium produced must be swept out or the fire smothers.
branches.cn: 残余：产生的氦必须扫出去，否则火会闷灭。

intro.en: The phrase joins the Latin kernel word to a Latin noun of pouring, so both halves describe the same act of merging.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的「果仁」接到拉丁语的「倾倒」名词上，两半都在描述同一个合并动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundere and fusio also yield fuse, fusion, confuse and refuse; Latin nucleus yields nuclear and nucleic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fundere 与 fusio 还衍生出 fuse、fusion、confuse、refuse；拉丁 nucleus 衍生 nuclear 与 nucleic。

items.example: The nucleus supplies the fuel.
items.exampleCN: 原子核提供燃料。

items.example: The verb describes separate pieces flowing into one.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述分开的块流成一体。

items.example: The noun names the act of merging.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指合并的动作。

items.example: The fusion of two companies created one firm.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司的合并造出一家公司。

items.example: Nuclear fusion powers the stars.
items.exampleCN: 核聚变为恒星供能。

items.example: The fusion reactor held the plasma for seconds.
items.exampleCN: 聚变堆把等离子体约束了几秒。

items.example: The thermonuclear explosion was detected at once.
items.exampleCN: 热核爆炸立刻被探测到。

items.example: The two wires fused in the heat.
items.exampleCN: 两根导线在高温中熔在一起。

latinEntries.structure: fundere, fundo, fudi, fusum (v., third conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to pour, to melt, to cast

definition_zh: 核裂变；重原子核裂成两个较轻核并释放能量与中子的过程
definition_en: the splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus into two lighter nuclei, releasing energy and neutrons
core_image: 一颗沉重的核被一颗小弹丸敲中，晃了一下，随后从中间断成两半，还弹出几颗小弹丸
scene: 反应堆里重核裂开，热量推动汽轮机。Nuclear fission in the reactor releases heat that drives the turbines.
sceneCN: 这里 nuclear fission 指「重核裂成较轻核并放出能量」（第 1 个义项：重原子核分裂的核反应）；句意：反应堆中的核裂变释放出热，热又推动汽轮机。图中可辨识物件：燃料棒、慢化水池、蒸汽管、汽轮机。

senses.title: A heavy nucleus splitting in two
senses.definition: the nuclear reaction in which a heavy nucleus divides into two lighter nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 重原子核分成两个较轻原子核的核反应
senses.example: Uranium-235 is the usual fuel for nuclear fission.
senses.exampleCN: 铀二三五通常是核裂变的燃料。
senses.why: Latin fission means 'a splitting', and the nucleus is literally divided into two large fragments.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义是「裂开」，原子核确实被分成两大块碎片。

senses.title: One splitting event and its energy
senses.definition: a single act of division by one nucleus, releasing a fixed amount of energy
senses.definitionCN: 某一个核发生的一次分裂，放出固定数量的能量
senses.example: Each nuclear fission releases about two hundred million electron volts.
senses.exampleCN: 每次核裂变约释放两亿电子伏特。
senses.why: The process is countable at the level of individual nuclei, so the phrase also names one event.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程在单个核的层面可数，因此这个短语也指一次事件。

senses.title: The self-sustaining chain
senses.definition: a chain reaction in which each fission releases neutrons that trigger further fissions
senses.definitionCN: 每次裂变放出的中子又触发更多裂变的连锁反应
senses.example: A chain reaction begins when enough fission events occur together.
senses.exampleCN: 当裂变事件足够密集地同时发生，链式反应便开始。
senses.why: Each split frees neutrons that can split neighbours, so one event can multiply into many.
senses.whyCN: 每次分裂都放出能劈开邻近核的中子，于是一次事件能增殖成许多次。

senses.title: The heat of a power reactor
senses.definition: the controlled fission in a reactor whose heat produces steam and electricity
senses.definitionCN: 反应堆中受控的裂变，其热产生蒸汽与电力
senses.example: The reactor controls nuclear fission so that heat stays steady.
senses.exampleCN: 反应堆控制核裂变，使热量保持稳定。
senses.why: Slow, controlled splitting turns an explosive reaction into a steady furnace.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢而受控的分裂把爆炸性反应变成稳定的熔炉。

senses.title: The atomic bomb
senses.definition: an uncontrolled fission chain reaction releasing energy in a fraction of a second
senses.definitionCN: 在不到一秒内释放能量的不受控裂变链式反应
senses.example: The first atomic bomb used nuclear fission for its entire yield.
senses.exampleCN: 第一颗原子弹的全部当量都来自核裂变。
senses.why: The same chain reaction, allowed to run wild, becomes a weapon rather than a power source.
senses.whyCN: 同一条链式反应若放任失控，便成为武器而非能源。

senses.title: The fragments left behind
senses.definition: the lighter nuclei produced by fission, many of them radioactive and long-lived
senses.definitionCN: 裂变产生的较轻核，其中许多具放射性且寿命很长
senses.example: Nuclear fission produces isotopes that remain dangerous for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 核裂变产生的同位素会在数十年间保持危险。
senses.why: The word for the act also names its products, because the split halves are the physical remains.
senses.whyCN: 指动作的词也指产物，因为裂开的两半就是留下的实体。

senses.title: Splitting without a trigger
senses.definition: the rare spontaneous division of a heavy nucleus without absorbing a neutron
senses.definitionCN: 重核未吸收中子便自行分裂的罕见情形
senses.example: Spontaneous nuclear fission sets a natural limit on heavy elements.
senses.exampleCN: 自发核裂变为重元素设下天然上限。
senses.why: Some nuclei are so unstable that they split on their own, without any incoming particle.
senses.whyCN: 有些核太不稳定，无需任何外来粒子也会自行裂开。

senses.title: The barrier that must be overcome
senses.definition: the energy threshold that keeps a nucleus stable until it is reached
senses.definitionCN: 使原子核在达到之前保持稳定的能量门槛
senses.example: The fission barrier explains why most heavy nuclei do not split at once.
senses.exampleCN: 裂变势垒解释了多数重核为何不会立刻裂开。
senses.why: A nucleus resists division until enough energy deforms it past the point of no return, so the threshold itself became a named concept.
senses.whyCN: 原子核在获得足够能量、变形到无法回头之前一直抗拒分裂，因此这道门槛本身成了一个有名字的概念。

intro.en: Nuclear fission joins the Latin kernel word to Latin fissio 'a splitting', from findere 'to split'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nuclear fission 把拉丁语的「果仁」接到拉丁 fissio「裂开」上，而 fissio 出自 findere「劈开」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Findere meant 'to split, to cleave', and it supplies the image of one body becoming two.
items.cn: findere 意为「劈开、裂开」，提供的是一体变两体的意象。

items.en: Fissio named a cleaving or a division, an action noun built on the same verb.
items.cn: fissio 指劈开或分开，是构于同一动词的动作名词。

items.en: English first used fission for the division of living cells, a sense still current in biology.
items.cn: 英语最初用 fission 指活细胞的分裂，这一义项在生物学里仍在使用。

items.en: When uranium bombarded with neutrons was found to split into lighter elements, the biological word was borrowed for the nucleus.
items.cn: 当被中子轰击的铀被发现裂成更轻的元素时，这个生物学词被借到了原子核上。

items.en: Controlled fission gave reactors, uncontrolled fission gave weapons, and fission products entered the language of waste.
items.cn: 受控裂变带来反应堆，失控裂变带来武器，裂变产物则进入废物管理的语汇。

items.en: The first uses of the exact phrase are approximate; the Latin chain and the 1938 discovery are well recorded.
items.cn: 这个确切短语最早的使用年代为约数；拉丁语链条与 1938 年的发现都有充分记录。

note.en: Group one holds split-root words plus the opposite reaction; group two holds words for the division, its timing and its products.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「劈开」词根的词，外加相反的反应；第二组是关于分裂、其时序与产物的词。

entries.definition: The general word for splitting, still used of cell division; the nuclear phrase restricts it to heavy nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指分裂，仍用于细胞分裂；核短语把它限定在重核。

entries.definition: A narrow opening or crack in rock or tissue, from the same cleaving verb but naming a gap rather than an act.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或组织中的窄缝，同出「劈开」动词，但指缝隙而非动作。

entries.definition: Capable of being split by neutrons; it describes the material, not the reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 能被中子劈开的；它描述材料，而非反应。

entries.definition: From a pouring verb rather than a splitting one: light nuclei joining instead of a heavy nucleus dividing.
entries.definitionCN: 出自「倾倒」而非「劈开」的动词：轻核结合，而非重核分裂。

entries.definition: Light nuclei joining to release energy; it is the opposite nuclear route and powers the stars.
entries.definitionCN: 轻核结合释放能量；它是相反的核路线，并为恒星供能。

entries.definition: A self-sustaining series of reactions; nuclear fission can become one when enough neutrons survive.
entries.definitionCN: 自持的一连串反应；当足够多中子存活时，核裂变便能成为链式反应。

entries.definition: One element becoming another; fission achieves it by splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter ones.
entries.definitionCN: 一种元素变成另一种；裂变通过把重核劈成较轻核来实现这一点。

entries.definition: A broad word for falling apart; it covers fission but does not distinguish the two large fragments.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指碎裂；它涵盖裂变，却不区分那两大块碎片。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin nucleus 'kernel' plus fissio 'a splitting': the kernel split in two.
normal.cn: 拉丁「果仁」加「裂开」：果仁裂成两半。

normal.en: The family runs nuclear fission, fission, fissile, fissionable, fission product.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括核裂变、裂变、易裂变的、可裂变的、裂变产物。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: induced nuclear fission, fission chain reaction, fission product.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：诱发核裂变、裂变链式反应、裂变产物。

normal.en: Fission splits; fusion pours together. The two words differ by one image.
normal.cn: 裂变分开，聚变倒在一起；两个词只差一个意象。

normal.en: Fissile material is the material that can be split; the word is an adjective, not the event.
normal.cn: 易裂变材料指能被劈开的材料；那是个形容词，不是事件。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy stone struck once and breaking into two halves that each fly off.
abstract.cn: 想象一块重石被敲一下，断成两半各自飞开。

abstract.en: Picture a line of dominoes where each fall pushes two more.
abstract.cn: 想象一排骨牌，每倒一张就推倒两张。

abstract.en: Picture a locked box that will not open until it is struck hard enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁住的箱子，敲得不够重就打不开。

examples.en: Nuclear fission was discovered by bombarding uranium with neutrons.
examples.cn: 核裂变是通过用中子轰击铀而被发现的。

examples.en: A reactor slows neutrons so that nuclear fission stays controlled.
examples.cn: 反应堆让中子减速，使核裂变保持受控。

examples.en: Nuclear fission leaves products that must be stored for centuries.
examples.cn: 核裂变留下的产物必须存放数百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nuclear（核的）+ fission（分裂）」——核一分为二，就是核裂变

root: nuclear（拉丁 nucleus「果仁、核」）+ fission（拉丁 fissio「裂开」← findere「劈开」）。英语 nuclear fission。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one heavy nucleus breaking: the split itself, a single event, the chain, reactor heat, the bomb, the fragments, spontaneous splitting and the barrier that delays it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一个重核的断裂展开：分裂本身、单次事件、链式反应、反应堆的热、炸弹、碎片、自发分裂，以及拖延它的势垒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy kernel struck by a small pellet, wobbling, then breaking into two halves that fly apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗重核被小弹丸敲中，晃了一下，随后断成两半各自飞开。

branches.en: PROCESS AND INSTANCE: the general reaction and one nucleus's division are the same break at two magnifications.
branches.cn: 过程与单例：一般反应与某一个核的分裂，是同一次断裂的两种放大。

branches.en: CONTROL: the chain can run wild or be held steady, and holding it steady produces power.
branches.cn: 控制：链可以失控，也可以被稳住，而稳住它便产生电力。

branches.en: THE TWO AFTERMATHS: the same chain becomes a bomb, and the split halves become long-lived waste.
branches.cn: 两种后果：同一条链成为炸弹，裂开的两半成为长寿命废物。

branches.en: THE UNPROMPTED SPLIT: some nuclei need no neutron and divide on their own.
branches.cn: 无人触发的分裂：有些核不需要中子，自己就会分。

branches.en: THE LOCK: a threshold of energy keeps most heavy nuclei whole until it is crossed.
branches.cn: 锁：一道能量门槛在越过多前使多数重核保持完整。

intro.en: The phrase joins the Latin kernel word to a Latin noun of cleaving, and the second half also gives fissure and fissile.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的「果仁」接到拉丁语的「劈开」名词上，后半还衍生出 fissure 与 fissile。

latinIntro.en: Latin findere and fissio also yield fissure, fissile and fissure in geology; Latin nucleus yields nuclear and nucleic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 findere 与 fissio 还衍生出 fissure、fissile 以及地质学里的裂缝一词；拉丁 nucleus 衍生 nuclear 与 nucleic。

items.example: The nucleus is the body that splits.
items.exampleCN: 原子核就是裂开的那个实体。

items.example: The verb describes one body becoming two.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述一体变两体。

items.example: The noun names the act of cleaving.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指劈开的动作。

items.example: Cell fission produces two daughter cells.
items.exampleCN: 细胞分裂产生两个子细胞。

items.example: Nuclear fission releases neutrons as well as heat.
items.exampleCN: 核裂变既放出热也放出中子。

items.example: Only certain isotopes are fissile.
items.exampleCN: 只有某些同位素是易裂变的。

items.example: Water entered through a narrow fissure.
items.exampleCN: 水从一条窄缝进入。

items.example: The fission product must be stored safely.
items.exampleCN: 裂变产物必须安全存放。
